Due to the intervention of Thor, this reality was split into two: one where the Twisters lived and one where they were terminated before they could hatch. In the reality in which they were destroyed, He Who Remains created the Time-Keepers to replace the Time-Twisters and to safeguard the next cycle of time. After their birth, the Time-Keepers traveled through time seeking ever-greater knowledge of the continuum and how it had produced them. They swiftly came to the conclusion that humanity was the gravest danger to their continued existence and decided that it would have to be contained. The Time-Keepers subsequently visited Immortus in Limbo and recruited him to monitor all time travel between 3000 BC and 4000 AD, as well as to untangle the time-travel mess his prior selves had left in their wake, and to serve as their agent in doing whatever they deemed necessary to safeguard the timestream. At some point, the Time-Twisters returned and were able to imprison and replace the Time-Keepers. Then, by assuming the likenesses of the Time-Keepers, the Time-Twisters were able to trick Immortus into unknowingly helping them carry out their plan to alter timelines so that their reality would be dominant and the one of the Time-Keepers would fade. However, when the Time-Twisters were eventually defeated, the true Time-Keepers were freed, enabling them to appear in the Citadel at the End of Time, closely followed by the disguised Time-Twisters whose faces immediately melted away, revealing their true forms. As the Time-Twisters melted into spherical blobs of matter, the Time-Keepers revealed their origin to the Watcher and explained how the Time-Twisters had deceived Immortus. With the Twisters now back in their nurture-pods, the Time-Keepers vowed to watch over them and ensure they would never hatch again. On one occasion, the Time-Keepers traveled to Chronopolis and secretly entered the chamber where Kang lay comatose in a Life Suspension Tube. As they looked upon him, Ast mentioned that Kang's eight millennium empire would face the single greatest threat to its continued existence that day and Kang was totally oblivious. Then, after all the Time-Keepers had removed their masks, Ast spoke to Vort, saying that in half the divergent timelines, this was the day that Chronopolis would fall and that reality would henceforth be demarcated by the event that would transpire later that day. Vort replied to Ast, saying that he was aware of that, and that divergences as significant as this one were rare. When one of the others mentioned that perhaps those timelines without Kang would flourish and predominate the continuum, Vort mentioned that he was greatly tempted to revive Kang himself, stating that it was in their best interests because the passing of Chronopolis would diminish the realm of their influence. However, a surprised Zanth firmly opposed that idea, pointing out that direct intervention in the course of events by beings with temporal powers as vast as theirs could cause chrono-synclastic entropy to engulf the entire sector. Vort quickly assured Zanth that he had merely been musing aloud and had not meant to inspire interpersonal uncertainty. Zanth then called out to Ast and Vort to draw their attention to the approach of a quasi-sentient entity, Kang's mechanical servant, Brideshead. Eventually, the Time-Keepers, while at their Citadel at the End of Time, attempted to use their chrono-cannon, powered by the Forever Crystal, to reorder all time at once in order to end the threat that humanity posed to the multiverse by wiping out all but the minimum number of timelines that were needed to preserve their own existence. However, they were opposed there by Immortus, whom they killed, Rick Jones and the team of Avengers who had been gathered to protect him, Libra, the Kree Supreme Intelligence and Kang, who had all become involved in the Destiny War. After Jones, empowered by the Destiny Force, destroyed their chrono-cannon, the Time-Keepers were left in a weakened state, and Kang took that opportunity to kill them all before they could escape.
powers: Allegedly all derived from their technology
transportation: Unspecified technology that enabled Ast to travel through time and between realities
fields.notes: Throughout most of their appearances, the Time-Keepers were known only by their group's name. The only exception was the story in , which not only revealed their individual names but also established that their supposed faces were actually masks that concealed the fact that they were all blue-skinned beings with large yellow eyes. On the second page of that issue, all three Time-Keepers were shown, for the first and only time, holding their masks in their hands. The Time-Keeper on the left was shown holding a green mask with two antennae attached. The fact that he addressed his words to "Vort" established that he was either Ast or Zanth. The Time-Keeper in the middle was shown holding a yellow mask. He responded to the first Time-Keeper's words, establishing that he was "Vort" and the first speaker was "Ast." The Time-Keeper on the right was shown holding a smooth blue mask. By a process of elimination, he must have been "Zanth." The fact that Ast was the Time-Keeper who seemed to have antennae on his forehead and green skin was confirmed by the profile on the Time-Keepers that appeared in . That profile does not mention that the "faces" of the Time-Keepers were actually masks, but that idea is somewhat supported by a profile on Timequake that was published in . The image created for that profile does show the three Time-Keepers in the upper right corner, all holding their masks in their hands. However, the masks are all green, and the Time-Keepers are depicted as having pinkish-white (Caucasian) skin and black eyes instead of blue skin and yellow eyes. Given that this profile is not an in-universe document and thus has no effect on continuity, this coloring inconsistency probably does count as a continuity error. In , the Supreme Intelligence revealed that the Time-Keepers were not gods, but mortal beings who possessed astounding technology. Kang repeated this in the following issue ( ), reminding the Time-Keepers that they were "only men with powerful machines" just before he murdered them. This would suggest that they should not be considered to be true Cosmic Beings.

astarta.name: Astarta
astarta.origin: Astarta was a beautiful princess of Mu who was ordered to become the bride of the sea-god her people worshiped. On the day she was to be married, her husband gave her eternal life, and she returned home. Many years later, the Great Cataclysm happened, and Astarta's husband saved her from death. She was brought to the island of Kelka where its people worshiped Astarta as a god. Kelka's priests, however, feared her and locked her away in a tower. Millennia went by, and the people of Kelka became more savage, and Astarta was tortured. Astarta was found by Conan the Cimmerian and his companion Bêlit. After Bêlit killed the evil priest Akkheba, Astarta was able to communicate with her husband the sea-god. In anger for the way Astarta was treated, the sea-god destroyed Kelka and its people. Astarta died as well, but this allowed her to join her husband.

aster.name: Aster
aster.origin: Aster was a fairy exiled from Otherworld for unknown reasons and a member of the Atelier, a secret and exclusive society of assassins. Aster was present when the group hosted Deadpool and Lady Deathstrike's audition to enter the Atelier. After numerous failures of the two and the betrayal of one of the members, Valentine Vuong, The Horned Emperor, Atelier's leader, assigned to all the members of the group a quest to find and kill them. She attacked Deadpool along with Alcaudón, by creating an illusion to trick them and retrieve his dog Princess; Alcaudón succeded, but Deadpool managed to kill Aster by pouring salt on her.

asteros.name: Asteros
asteros.origin: ===Origin=== Asteros was a deity, the son of Chaos, and a god of light. ===Modern Age=== The Calefaction of Asteros was a medallion bathing its wielder's body and soul in warmth, and that was found in ruins under Atlantis after a great upheaval by an Atlantean. The pendant caused him to go sick, and the induced fever preventing him from working, leading him to be a homeless beggar, in which state he kept the Calefaction of Asteros on him as it still provided him warmth.

fields.notes: Astaroth, also known as Asteroth, was (in demonology) the Great Duke of Hell, derived from Ishtar and Astarte. Asteroth, created in (May, 2005; written by Mike Oeming and Daniel Berman, and penciled by Andrea Di Vito), as a "cosmic demon" from the beginning of creation, imprisoned for eons, is inspired by the Cthulhu Mythos. She was later listed as an Old One in a subnote about Hoggoth in "The Inner Planes" section of "Planes Prelude" ( ; August, 2007), and in the Demons' profile in (September, 2007), and then either as a Lesser Old One or a Great Old One in the update Demons' profile in (July, 2008) In "Blossoms of the Black Lotus", in and "There Will Come a Dark Stranger", in (both written by Don Kraar), Conan invokes Asteroth's name. It is possibly another mistake (or an alternate name) on naming Ashtoreth (another name of Ishtar).

asti.origin: thumb|left|Asti stealing the Evil Eye from the Defenders and Avengers ===Preface=== Asti was a demonic creature that has served as a minion of Dormammu. Asti the All-Seeing was also worshiped on Sutarnilia, a planet of the Dark Dimension, as the God of Candor, from which no falsehood could hide. Once a year, the Sutarnilians organized the False Face of Asti the All-Seeing, a festival where they wore masks ressembling Asti's face, and offered as tribute a week of "fearless honesty." ===Modern Age=== Asti was once set upon Doctor Strange who was able to defeat the creature. Later, during the Avengers/Defenders War, Dormammu sent Asti to collect the completed Evil Eye from the two hero teams in order merge the Dark Dimension with Earth's dimension. While Asti succeeded in its task, Dormammu's plot ultimately failed. Asti was later recruited by the Maker to join his New Revengers.

astra mutant.name: Astra (Mutant)
astra mutant.origin: Not much has been revealed about the history and origin of the woman known only as Astra. She claims to have been an original recruit for the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants, led by the self-proclaimed mutant ruler, Magneto. According to personnel data from Orchis, Astra joined a mission in California that resulted in the death of the parents of Orchis agent Jun Wei. Astra left the group under mysterious circumstances before it made its first public appearance fighting the mutant group called the X-Men. She claimed that Magneto "emotionally beat" her. She continued to track Magneto's subsequent activities. Her fascination with Magneto led her to create a sophisticated clone of him, one that was "created to be even stronger than Magneto, lacking the self-restraint Magneto placed on his powers years ago." However, in order to create the clone, Astra had to restore the health of the real Magneto, who had been placed in a catatonic state by Professor Xavier. Magneto, once restored, fought the clone and the battle ranged to South America, where he defeated the clone and fled. The clone found a name for himself, Joseph, and soon found himself with the X-Men, developing relationships with them. Presumably during this time, Astra was consumed with other plans, or was otherwise occupied elsewhere. Astra first made herself known by re-capturing Joseph when he was wandering in the Israeli desert, believing himself to be the real Magneto. Astra revealed her hand in Joseph's creation. She then used Joseph to infiltrate Magneto's base, at a time when Magneto was trying to realign the Earth's electromagnetic spectrum as a part of his war against humanity. Attempting to kill Magneto in order to be seen as Earth's savior, Astra wanted to use Joseph to control the energies that Magneto had tapped into. Joseph, however, after defeating Magneto, ended up repairing the damage to the magnetosphere by merging with it. Astra was defeated by the X-Men's Nightcrawler, whom she professed to recognize from his youth. She used her teleportation powers to escape, vowing to return and face the X-Men again. It was assumed she was killed by Apocalypse, but she survived. thumb|left|280px|Stepford Cuckoos (Earth-616)|The Cuckoos probe Astra's mind Astra kept her powers after the Decimation. She restored Joseph's body and together they formed a new Brotherhood. They fought with Magneto, and as a result, Astra was caught and locked in the X-Brig on Utopia. ===House of X=== Astra was eventually welcomed to the new mutant island of Krakoa, created by Xavier, Magneto, and Moira X. She entered through the teleportation gateway alongside other villainous and fractious mutants, who had been invited to join the nation in order to heal mutantdom and start over as a whole species together.

astra polemachus.name: Astra (Polemachus)
astra polemachus.origin: When the energy rings above Polemachus started increasing, endangering its people, a group of priests, led by Anskar decided to perform human sacrifices to appease to gods. Astra was chosen to be sacrificed. But before she could be sacrificed, Thundra and Arkon rescued her and escaped to Earth, where they encountered the Avengers. Anskar then teleported the three along with the Avengers back to Polemachus. Before Anskar could kill Astra, the Avengers intervened and offered to investigate the rings. In the end, while the Avengers restored the rings, Anskar still believed the only solution was a sacrifice to the gods, so he killed Astra.

Anskar then teleported the three along with the Avengers back to Polemachus. Before Anskar could kill Astra, the Avengers intervened and offered to investigate the rings. In the end, while the Avengers restored the rings, Anskar still believed the only solution was a sacrifice to the gods, so he killed Astra.

astreas.name: Astreas
astreas.origin: Astreas was a historian, chronicler and probably a philosopher. He and his fellow philosopher Alcemides were native of Nemedia. Astreas reported the events happened in Khauran. He had gotten a correspondence with Alcemides, and probably Alcemides used some of Astreas' informations to write his Nemedian Chronicles. Astreas was really surprised from the changes happened from Constantius arrival in Khauran. He asked himself if the Queen was possessed by a demon, and was quite sure that Conan wasn't dead but rode at the flank of Olgerd Vladislav and his Zuagirs. Astreas also spoke to Marcios, a soldier, who was sure that the Queen was a witch and that Taramis was alive but imprisoned. Astreas went to live in a camp of tents, some miles outside Khauran, and from there sent his letters using carrier-pigeons.

astrid bloom.name: Astrid Bloom
astrid bloom.origin: Astrid grew up as a normal child, with her loving mother and father, in England. When she was a child, her father passed away. Nine month later, Astrid's mom met a man by the name of Aubrey Chilton and got married. Astrid had mixed feeling about her mom's sudden remarriage, but found it in her heart to accept the new couple. Her mother and stepfather had another child not long after, giving her a new sister, Yvonne. The changes happened rapidly, switching Astrid's room into a nursery while she slept on the couch. As years went by, Astrid become increasingly depressed, resentful, and enraged. When she reached the age of thirteen, her telepathic abilities activated. Bloom claimed her mother favored Astrid's half-sister Yvonne over her, later sending her away after learning of her powers. Emma later found that Astrid's purported background history was a fraud; in truth, Astrid had mind-controlled Yvonne into killing their parents. Yvonne was sent to a mental institution shortly thereafter. Astrid then moved to New York City. This taught Astrid to depend on herself. It is unknown how she was accepted to Empire State University, but there she met Emma Frost, who she found to be a mutant as well. Astrid taught Emma how to use her powers. Astrid became closer to Emma, as a sister. They told each other everything, though deep down inside, Astrid was planning an evil scheme to bring down Emma. She had also been subtly manipulating Emma in order turn her against both men and non-mutant humanity. Astrid controlled the mind of Ian (Emma's boyfriend at the time) and made him act like a chauvinistic bigot. Emma soon found out that Astrid was making Ian do wicked things. Though she tried to explain to Emma that she did it so he would not break her heart in the future, Emma saw through Astrid's false sincerity. In a desperate effort to control Emma, while simultaneously framing Emma's boyfriend for assault; Bloom attempted to temporarily imprison Emma by trapping Frost's psyche within her own psyche. This however proved to be a disastrous strategy to use against another telepath, as it allowed Emma to instantly review and assimilate all of Astrid's memories, knowledge, skills, and abilities, including all she knew about telepathic utilization and combat. Now armed with the technical skill to back up her far superior power level; Emma freed herself, then confronted and psionically lashed out against an incredulous Astrid. The confrontation was short, with Bloom having never stood a chance. Astrid was left catatonic by Emma who seemingly destroyed her mind. It is unknown whether Astrid lost her powers in M-Day.

astrid josefsen.name: Astrid Josefsen
astrid josefsen.origin: Astrid was the granddaughter of Harald Josefsen, the man who would eventually become the Mad Viking, self proclaimed destroyer of "wussy men" who didn't match up to his macho ideals. She became a victim of his rage after she was about to leave on a date with a man that didn't measure up to the Viking's idea. She was chased into the swamps outside Citrusville. There, she witnessed the Viking slaughter shock-rocker Star Spangler and his followers before she was saved by the Man-Thing. She fled and called the police, which started a man-hunt for her crazed grandfather. However, the Viking soon became associated with the Mothers for Decency, who led an angry mob to Citrusville High School to burn textbooks which they blamed for the state of the world today. While attempting to stop them with Richard Rory, she tried to make her grandfather see sense by trying to make him realize she was a product of his upbringing. In response to this, he killed her. Shortly after, he met his own end at the hands of the Man-Thing.

astrid mordo.name: Astrid Mordo
astrid mordo.origin: Astrid used magic to transfer her father's cancer into Dr. Strange. She then invaded the home of the Ancient One and took him and his monks captive in order to drain their powers. Baron Mordo was also there and she and her father went home to Castle Mordo. Once Dr. Strange realized he had Mordo's cancer, he went to the Ancient One's monastery to find Mordo. Astrid sent a demon to subdue Strange and bring him to Castle Mordo. A weakened Strange tried to attack her, but she defeated him. She shot magical energy knives at him hoping to kill him, but they were blocked by her father. Tricking his daughter into thinking he wanted to kill Strange himself, he transferred his cancer back into his own body to let Strange fight Astrid. Dr. Strange teleported the monks away, and Astrid summoned demons to attack him. Once he was done fighting the demons, Astrid teleported Strange's friends Amanda and Jessica to her side. She threatened to kill them if Strange did not surrender, which he did. Baron Mordo sneaked up and stabbed Astrid in the back with a magic knife which put her in a coma. He then cast her body into another dimension, so she could never hurt anyone again.

astriel.name: Astriel
astriel.origin: Astriel is a native who lived in an unnamed realm that is home to a race of immortals that existed a polar realm within the Frozen North during the Hyborian Age. She met and fell in love with a fellow warrior named Kendrick. Unwilling to watch the man she loved die a day at a time, as mortal men do, she used a spell to keep his youth forever, as long as he stayed within the boundaries of her realm. Years later, Astriel was suddenly abducted by the wizard Thoth-Amon from her native realm, and brought to Stygia. Seeking to obtain her vast power he used spells and physical torture, in an attempt to break her spirit and bind her to his will. Astriel resisted fiercely, but her defeat would have been inevitable had she not been rescued by Kendrick.

astro.name: Astro
astro.origin: Astro was an astrology student from ancient Mesopotamia (modern Iraq). He was using an apparently inactive volcano as an observation point to study the night sky. However, the volcano eventually erupted and Astro was there during the eruption. He tried to escape, but he was instead sealed in a nearby cave. Astro was mutated by the explosion, gaining shape-shifting powers. He remained trapped in the cave for thousands of years, in an apparent state of inertia. In the modern era, a new eruption of the volcano released Astro from his captivity. He was shocked at realizing what happened to him. Lashing out in anger, he destroyed several Middle Eastern cities. After calming down, he started traveling the globe. He eventually settled in the United States of America. Despite his powers keeping him alive for so long, Astro still had a need to eat and drink to remain alive. This forced him to find a job and start earning an income. He uses his expertise in astrology to be hired as an astrology columnist by the Daily Bugle. He used a feminine form to assume the identity of "Jane Virgo". Astro used the super-villain identity of "Mr. Zodiac" in a series of clashes with Spider-Man, while using the identity of "Jane Virgo" to befriend Peter Parker. Peter shared his theories about Mr. Zodiac with "Jane", and eventually noticed that the villain seemed to change plans according to the information only Peter and Jane knew about. After injuring Mr. Zodiac in a battle, Spidey noticed a similar injury on "Jane". Allowing him to deduce the villain's identity. After Peter became aware of her true identity, Jane kidnapped Peter's acquaintance of "Ben". She started blackmailing Peter over Ben's safety. By this point, Peter had noticed that the villain required several minutes of concentration for their powers to properly work. He contacted Ben and had him intentionally disrupting Jane's concentration. With Astro's powers unavailable to him due to the constant disruptions, these powers stopped keeping him alive. Astro/Jane's body collapsed into mere dust. J. Jonah Jameson was frustrated that Jane disappeared without a trace. He accused Peter Parker of doing something to drive her off.

astron.name: Astron
astron.origin: Astron, like every Eternal, was created by the Celestials. 400,000 years later, a civil war erupted between two factions of the Eternals: the side of Kronos, who cherished piece and non-interference, and the side of Uranos, wanting to use their powers to dominate the planet. Astron joined Uranos' side, but they were defeated by Kronos' forces and banished from the Earth. When the two dozen exiles landed on the planet Uranus, they conquered the Kree outpost there to make of it their new home. As the Eternal Uranos built a spaceship to return to Earth, Astron refused to follow his ways any longer and, along with three sympathizers, remained on the planet Uranus, where they created their own colony. He and the other Uranian Eternals were presumably killed by Deathurge when he pierced their protective dome. After his death, Astron was resurrected on Earth, in the Exclusion, and eventually joined Oceanus' Oceanic Watch.

astronomica.name: Astronomica
astronomica.origin: Astronomica was a space explorer the Fantastic Four encountered during one of their adventures. When the heroes were returning to Earth, they took a wrong turn and ended up in the Crossroads of Infinity which risked them not being able to return home. Astronomica lent the Fantastic Four her Stellarex Stone, an artifact which could show the way to a person's home they sang to it. The rest of the team volunteered their best singer, the Human Torch, to use it. He was successful, and the gem lit a path to Earth. astyanax.name: Astyanax
astyanax.origin: Astyanax was the son of Hector (and thus the grandson of Priam, king of Troy) and of Andromache. In the morning after the Achaeans sacked the city (after having entered it using a wooden horse full of their warriors), the Trojans were rounded up, and Achaean strategist Odysseus, supported by the seer Calchas, stated that Astyanax, as the son of Hector (killed earlier in the war by Achilles), was to be killed to prevent him from avenging his parents and city, and so Odysseus tore him from his mother and threw him from the city's walls, despite Andromache's complaints. She fainted at her son's fall, only for Achilles' son Neoptolemus to claim her for himself.

asura deity.name: Asura (Deity)
asura deity.origin: ===Hyborian Age=== Asura was a new god. When the older god Yaamai, the four-armed god of death and sleep, used his trident, fire-sword, mace, and noose to conquer all, except for Asura. Asura defeated and bound him up, among others. Asura was worshiped in various countries: Asura was the popular deity in Vendhya, and its chief-deity. His Priests served the throne. Asura was seemingly also worshipped in Iranistan, in the Ilbars. Asura was worshiped in Aquilonia, as early as 10,000 BC, where it was tolerated, and the Followers of Aquilonia were protected by King Conan I, despite the pressure from the Priests of Mitra who wished to mount up an inquisition and purge them from Aquilonia. Kalligor sacrificed to him for favors. Asura was worshiped in the city later known as the City of the Plague. Most or all of his priests there died from the plague.

asylum psionex.name: Asylum (Psionex)
asylum psionex.origin: Asylum was hospitalized in a mental hospital for some reason, before being used by Genetech for their research in creating superhuman beings. She was given the name of Asylum and her powers, she participated as a member of Psionex during its early activities, such as battling with the young heroes of the New Warriors. Asylum and the other members of Psionex escaped from Genetech's facilities during Terrax's return. She later fought Nova and Speedball in Manhattan but was dispersed by Speedball leaving behind only her mask. Her mask was later used as a conduit from the Darkforce Dimension back to Earth by the Darkling, who took her mask a became the new Asylum. The original Asylum's whereabouts since then are unknown. An Asylum appeared with Psionex for the Maryland team for the 50-State Initiative, but their identity is uncertain.

atalis.name: Atalis
atalis.origin: Atalis claimed to be no sorcerer, but merely a philosopher, a seeker after knowledge. He survived this way the purge of all wizards in Yaralet, but the evil satrap Munthassem Khan cursed him with pain of convulsion. Looking in his crystal ball, he discovered that Conan was wearing the Heart of Tammuz, the counter-talisman for the Hand of Nergal wielded by Munthassem Khan, so he ordered his slave girl Hildico to bring the Cimmerian to him. The trio then confronted Munthassem Khan in his palace, and watched as the two artifacts released the essence of ancient colossal beings of light and darkness who began their eternal struggle anew. The being of light from the Heart of Tammuz won the battle. After Munthassem Khan's disintegration at the defeat of his patron, Prince Tann was crowned the new satrap and greeted Conan, who, after a week of relaxation, was ready to travel back to Turan again, but this time in the company of Hildico. ; Many years later, Conan and several other warriors traveled to Munthassem Khan's former quarters, where they were confronted by Atalis, who revealed his involvement with the cult of Nergal, as well as his warrior servant, Fafnir of the Demon Hand.

atar.name: Atar
atar.origin: ===Origin=== Allegedly, according to the ancient Zoroastrian lore, Ahura Mazda, the creator god, emerged from the personification of infinite time, Zurvan. A wise and benevolent being, representing truth, order and justice, Ahura Mazda started populating his domain with life. His birth was soon followed in the one of his twisted mirror image and antithesis, Ahriman, who personified deceit and chaos. Ahriman rejected the peace offerings of Ahura Mazda and tried to kill the life who had been imbued in his domain. After a prolonged battle, Ahura Mazda narrowly overcame and banished Ahriman to the Nether Realms. Atar, god of fire, was one of the Yazatas created by Ahura Mazda to uphold order and justice and in preparation for Ahriman's return. Also known as Agni, god of fire and purification, he was seemingly worshiped alongside with the Daevas, the Hindu gods. ===Worship=== The Yazatas ended up being worshiped on Earth in the Persian/Iranian plateau, as well as in Central Asia and India, from 1000 BC into modern days. The nexus between Earth and Elysium was indeed located on Mount Damavand in the Alborz Mountains and at Naqsh-e Rustam (within modern-day Iran).

atarah.name: Atarah
atarah.origin: After the planet Chronyca-2 was destroyed by Izel and her Shrike, Atarah assumed the leadership of the few surviving Chronicoms and began seeking for the way to prevent that tragedy through Time Travel. To that end she tasked Malachi with finding Leo Fitz, who was traveling in the company of Chronicom Enoch. Malachi successfully captured his target on Kitson and delivered him to Atarah, but was soon followed by Enoch in the company of the S.H.I.E.L.D. agents looking for Fitz. Jemma Simmons agreed to stay prisoner alongside Fitz, whom the Chronicoms wanted to develop a method of Time Travel, while the rest of their friends were let go. The Chronicom took complete brain scans of their prisoners, gaining full access to their memories, before they were rescued by Enoch. Malachi then felt that it was time for their people to establish Chronyca-3, but Atarah disagreed and Malachi killed her, taking control of the remaining Chronicom Hunters.

Likewise, Ataros is mentioned as the "brother to Hypnos and Thanatos." athena parthenos.name: Athena Parthenos
athena parthenos.origin: ===Origin=== 250px|thumb|left|Birth of Athena Athena was the daughter of the Titaness Metis and Zeus, He impregnated her, before he was foretold by the Fates that their child would be greater than him. Zeus consequently consumed Metis in an attempt to prevent that prophecy. Nine months later, Zeus was afflicted with violent headaches. Hephaestus trephined him, giving birth to a fully grown and armored Athena. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Medusa, Euryale and Stheno, daughters of Phorcys and Ceto worshiped Olympian gods rather than their grandfather Set. Medusa was a chaste priestess of Athena, as were her sisters, having all taken a vow of celibacy. Despite her vow, she was seduced by Poseidon and fell to his advances on Athena's altar. Enraged, Athena cursed the three sisters (and their descendants) as snake-haired creatures (possibly by releasing their true nature, as those features were shared by their aunt Ishiti and her offspring known as the Man-Serpents). ===Ancient Greece=== Athena later joined the Olympians on Olympus being worshiped by the humans of Ancient Greece. The city of Athens was named in her honor after she won a contest between her and her uncle, the sea-god Poseidon to decide who would lay claim to the city. Poseidon gave the people a salty spring to curry their favor but they ultimately chose Athena over Poseidon when the goddess provided an olive tree that was more useful. Thus, she became the patron goddess of Athens. ====Medusa and Perseus==== In 2000 BC, she led the hero Perseus to the location of Medusa. She gave him magical shield. After his success she carved the Gorgon's head on her shield. ====The Eternals==== Zeus discovered Olympia, home to the superhumanly long-lived offshoot of humanity known as the Eternals, who resided near the gods' home of Olympus itself. Olympia was the capital city of the Eternals and was ruled by Zuras. Zeus and Athena then traveled to Olympia to meet with Zuras and his daughter Azura, named after her father. Athena noticed the physical resemblances between Zeus and Zuras and herself and Azura and hence suggested a pact of non-interference between the two races, where the Olympian Eternals would act as the gods' heralds on Earth at certain times. The pact was sealed and Azura changed her name to Thena to honor the pact. ====Arachne==== Her brother Ares told Athena of a mortal woman, Arachne, who claimed to be a better weaver then her. This caused Athena to bring Arachne to Ares for judgement over daring to make herself appear better than the gods, and appeared to have been executed for this. Unbeknownst to the Olympians, Arachne was secretly a herald of the trickster god Anansi, and desiring justice for her ignited a war between them and the African gods. Once the war subsided, Athena felt guilt for what happened to Arachne and resurrected her into the form of a creature with a spider body instead of legs. ====Tiresias==== Tiresias once stumbled upon Athena while she was bathing. As a result, the goddess decided to blind him. His mother begged Athena to lift the curse, but she refused to. Instead, she opened Tiresias' ears so he might hear all the whispers of the Gods. This two curses/gifts gave him a greater perspective of the world. ====Hercules==== As the Fates had prophesized that no god could slay the giants, but a mortal bearing the lion's sign, Athena convinced Zeus to conceive such a creature, Hercules, which would give them the upper hand in the coming Gigantomachy. The city of Athens was named in her honor after she won a contest between her and her uncle, the sea-god Poseidon to decide who would lay claim to the city. This caused Athena to bring Arachne to Ares for judgement over daring to make herself appear better than the gods, and appeared to have been executed for this. Unbeknownst to the Olympians, Arachne was secretly a herald of the trickster god Anansi, and desiring justice for her ignited a war between them and the African gods. Once the war subsided, Athena felt guilt for what happened to Arachne and resurrected her into the form of a creature with a spider body instead of legs. ====Tiresias==== Tiresias once stumbled upon Athena while she was bathing. Ultimately, Hercules succeeded in slaying Kyknos. ====Trojan War==== Athena also participated in the Trojan War taking the side of the Greeks against the Trojans to avenge, at least in her mind, an insult performed on her by the Trojan prince Paris. athidel.name: Athidel
athidel.first_appearance: Marvel Super Hero Adventures: Frost Fight!
athidel.origin: He was patrolling Alfheim when Loki tricked him and Athidel was frozen by Ymir and forced to take the two villains to the cave where the Jorokraken guarded the Casket of Ancient Power. Loki stopped the Jorokraken and obtained the chest, though Athidel assured him that Jolnir was too powerful. Loki caused a landslide and escaped with Ymir. The Avengers with Malitri arrived and the heroes fought the Jorokraken until Athidel blew a whistle that stopped the monster's attack. Athidel allowed the Avengers to continue searching for Jolnir. Later, Athidel and Malitri were convinced by Reptil not to continue attacking the Avengers. Loki and Ymir arrived and Loki used his scepter to control Athidel and the other elves to attack the Avengers. The Avengers defeated Loki by freeing the elves, Athidel immobilized Loki and he was forced to rebuild Jolnir's home.

athmar phong.name: Athmar Phong
athmar phong.origin: Athmar Phong was a cruel magician who lived in Zangabal and belonged to an unnamed brotherhood. He possessed a mirror of black glass that was coveted by Kaman Thuu, a priest of the Seven Gods of Zangabal. Zangabal's Thieves' Guild refused to perform the deed, fearing Athmar Phong. Fleeing the city guard, the thief Thongor was offered sanctuary by Kaman Thuu to perform the task, as Athmar Phong was away reveling with his brotherhood. Kaman Thuu provided Thongor with the Shield of Cathloda, a protective talisman, and sent him on his way through tunnels towards Athmar Phong's house. Infiltrating the house, Thongor was taken captive by the Demon of Zangabal, who assumed the guise of a slave girl to seduce Thongor and take the Shield of Cathloda from him. Thongor was defeated and taken to Athmar Phong's dungeon, where he met with Ald Thurmis Thongor used his magic amulet to break the Mirror of Zaffar, unleashing the enraged demon imprisoned within the mirror who escaped and took Athmar Phong with him as he returned to the Ultracosmos.

athol kussar.name: Athol Kussar
athol kussar.origin: Athol Kussar was the CFO of the mining company owned by his half-brother, Faust Swart. The records of illicit transactions between Swart and Hydra were kept only in Kussar's memory, courtesy of his eidetic memory. Due to the importance of this information, S.H.I.E.L.D. tried to capture Kussar, but failed. After this event, Swart had Kussar imprisoned in a fortified cell below one of his radioactive mines. When S.H.I.E.L.D. operative Sue Storm Richards infiltrated Kussar's cell to retrieve him, using her force-fields to survive the radiation, she found the Mole Man trying to accomplish the same objective. Sue incapacitated the Mole Man and proceeded to break Kussar out of his cell; however, Hydra's safeguard had been activated due to this course of action, a bomb inside Kussar's body. Because of the emergency, Sue performed an open heart surgery on Kussar under the directions of Jemma Simmons. Even though she couldn't extract the explosive, she managed to seal off the explosive charge and ensure Kussar's safety. The Invisible Woman proceeded to take Kussar back to the surface and to the S.H.I.E.L.D. headquarters.

atlan.name: Atlan
atlan.origin: Atlan was a mystic and dolphin member of the Conspiracy who sought to gain immortality from the Exo-Mind. He was in possession of a Bloodgem fragment and was briefly introduced to Ulysses Bloodstone before they initiated the ritual to open the portal for the Exo-Mind. Instead of giving them what they desired, the Exo-Mind siphoned off the members souls, killing them and used them to transform the Bloodgem into a crystalline monster. When Ulysses' astral form traveled into the creature he discovered the souls of the Conspiracy. After the creatures destruction, the souls are presumed to have disipated. Sometime later, Captain America stumbled across their undisturbed corpses.

atlas olympian.name: Atlas (Olympian)
atlas olympian.origin: ===Overview=== Atlas is a member of the Titans a group of humanoid beings that hale from the pocket dimension; Olympus. He was condemned to hold up the sky for eternity by Zeus. He is also the Axis Mundi which moves around the Earth to wherever the spiritual and culture dominates at the time. ===Early Life=== He was born on Olympus, he was the son of Iapetus and Clymene, and brother of Prometheus, Epimetheus, and Menoetius. He sired the Pleiades (Maia, Alcyone, Electra, Celaeno, Sterope, Merope, and Taygete) with his wife Pleione, but also the Hesperides (Aegle, Erytheia, and Arethusa) with Hesperis and the Hyades (Coronis, Cleeia, Eudora, and Phaea) with Aethra. ===Titanomachy=== When Zeus rebelled against his father Chronus, Atlas and his army fought back against the young Olympians. The war became known as the Titanomachy, and lasted for almost 10 years. Zeus released the Titans' enemies from Tartarus, overwhelming Atlas and his forces. ===Punishment=== 250px|left|thumb|Axis Mundi (Cosmic Axis)|Axis Mundi When the Olympians defeated the Titans; Zeus the most powerful sent out two Eagles to mark the boundaries of his dominion. Where they met was declared the center of the world. It was there he condemned Atlas to hold the Heavens aloft as the Axis Mundi, the world Axis. The continent where he stood was christened "Atlantis" which simply meant the "Isle of Axis". ===Great Cataclysm=== In 18,000 BC, a group of sorcerers in Atlantis tried to harness the power of Omphalos the "navel of the axis" to control the turning of the Axis to make themselves the center of the world forever. This caused Atlas tremendous pain. The powerful energies wielded through the Omphalos caused the Great Cataclysm sinking Atlantis beneath the ocean. ===Golden Apples=== Gaea, goddess of Earth, gave Hera a tree of Golden Apples as a wedding present. Atlas' daughters had the role of protecting it. ===Encounter with Perseus=== The Axis Mundi shifted to the region that world that would one day be known as Morocco in Africa. A millennia later he encountered Perseus who was traveling through the region after slaying Gorgon; Medusa. The Hesperides offered him shelter on his long journey home. Perseus tried to take some Golden Apples as a gift for his mother. When Atlas saw him and tried to warn he used Medusa's head to turn him to stone. He was turned into the Atlas Mountains. ===Twelve Labors of Hercules=== 250px|left|thumb In 1268 BC, Hercules was ordered to fetch the golden apples from Atlas' daughters, so he asked Atlas for help. Atlas had Hercules hold up the heavens while Atlas went to look for his daughters, who had the apples. Finally Atlas returned, but he didn't want to take over holding up the sky again. He had enjoyed his brief break and told Hercules that he would deliver the apples himself to the king. Hercules tricked Atlas into taking the load back by asking Atlas to hold it while he shifted the load. Hercules then took the apples and Atlas again shouldered the weight of the heavens. Apparently, like Hercules, the Eternal Gilgamesh once took Atlas' burden on his own shoulders. ===528 BC=== In 528 BC, he stood over the Falgu River in India, as Siddartha Gautama attained enlightenment to become the great Buddha. ===1st Century BC=== In the first century BC, he passed over what would become Korea. ===18th Century=== 250px|thumb|Axis Mundi move to the Washington, D.C. On September 18th, 1793, the President of the United States of America, George Washington, was at a ceremony laying the cornerstone of the capital of the new city Washington, D.C.. atlez.origin: The being known as Atlez was the custodian of the Multiverse, his task was that of monitoring the various realities, keeping them maintained and preventing them tumbling into the Cosmic Abyss. Atlez died and was replaced by his successor Atleza.

atleza langunn.name: Atleza Langunn
atleza langunn.species: Human transformed into a Cosmic Being
atleza langunn.origin: thumb|left After the death of Atlez, Atleza took his place as a custodian of the Multiverse. It is her destiny to monitor the various realities while her very existence prevents it from tumbling into the Cosmic Abyss. She did not over oversee the entire Multiverse, but rather a vast subset of largely parallel realities. While noticing that all of her universes were decaying and dying, Atleza decided to task saving them to Deadpool and Wolverine who were best friends in every single one of her realities, except for Earth-616. However, her plan failed as instead of working together to save the universes, Earth-616 Deadpool and Wolverine decided to kill everyone they encountered in every alternate universe, which eventually led to all of them decaying and dying. Wolverine and Deadpool of Earth-616 eventually came face to face with Atleza, but by this point she had already given up on them. Instead, she summoned their Superior Variants who were 25% more handsome and also best friends with each other. Working together, they restored every universe, while Atleza unceremoniously dumped the Earth-616 ones back home.

However, her plan failed as instead of working together to save the universes, Earth-616 Deadpool and Wolverine decided to kill everyone they encountered in every alternate universe, which eventually led to all of them decaying and dying. Wolverine and Deadpool of Earth-616 eventually came face to face with Atleza, but by this point she had already given up on them. Instead, she summoned their Superior Variants who were 25% more handsome and also best friends with each other. Working together, they restored every universe, while Atleza unceremoniously dumped the Earth-616 ones back home.

atli wodendottir.name: Atli Wodendottir
atli wodendottir.origin: Atli is the youngest granddaughter of Thor, the king of Asgard. She along with her two sisters, Frigg and Ellisiv were captured by the god-butcher Gorr and taken to his slave planet forcing them along with other time-displaced gods to construct the Godbomb, a monolithic explosive that spells destruction of all gods. After spending an unknown amount of time there, Atli and her sisters came across a new slave brought to the planet, a very ill-tempered individual who unbeknownst to them, was a younger alternate version of their grandfather. Not realizing they were related, the hot-tempered Atli was in favor of castrating Thor - whose repeated attempts at rebellion resulted in Gorr crucifying other gods. Atli and her sisters planned a rebellion to destroy Gorr's Godbomb, but Thor stole their weapon and ineffectually attempted to use it. After Gorr's death, Atli and her sisters returned home and helped Thor fend off Galactus - claiming Jarnbjorn as her weapon of choice. Atli and her sisters helped Thor restore life on Earth, and were left in-charge of overseeing New Midgard. When Doom attacked, she and her sisters attempted to fend him off but was briefly captured. After being freed by her grandfather and Phoenix, she and her sisters protected the humans from Doom's monsters.

ator inhuman.name: Ator (Inhuman)
ator inhuman.origin: General Ator was the commander of the Crimson Cadre, an elite military force created by the Inhuman Genetic Council following the self-exile of the Inhuman Royal Family to Earth. Under his command were the flying Margoyle, the muck-man known as Glaboo, the electrically powered Pulssus, the tree man known as Rootar and the amphibious Eelak among others. The first recorded mobilization of the Crimson Cadre came when the Fantastic Four ventured to the moon to question the Watcher over his recent activities on Earth. General Ator demanded that the Fantastic Four be shot out of the sky due to their past assistance to the royal family in defying the Genetic Council. Although they lost track of the Fantastic Four's Stealth-Hawk ship, they were able to later track down the Thing later on the surface of the moon outside the Watcher's Citadel. They ambushed the Thing and nearly overpowered him until they were forced by Kristoff Vernard's retainer Boris who threatened to unleash the Stealth-Hawks weapons upon them. Ator ordered his troops to retreat, but vowed to get revenge against the Fantastic Four. Not long after this, the Watcher's citadel was swallowed up in a vortex accidentally activated by Nathaniel Richards, which threatened to destroy the Inhumans home of Attilan. This coincided with the sorceress Morgan Le Fay raising the continent of Atlantis to the surface of Earth's oceans. Seeking to reclaim their ancestral home, the Genetic Council abandoned the Inhumans to their fate and went to Earth. Meanwhile, the Crimson Cadre discovered that a human was responsible and after arming themselves with an Atmo-Gun, traveled to Earth to get revenge against the human race, launching an attack in Florida. After the Cadre left Attilan, it was saved by the Fantastic Four, who shrunk it down to size and took it aboard their ship the Stealth-Hawk. The group were opposed by the members of Fantastic Force who were able to disable the Atmo Gun and trap the Crimson Cadre within a Negative Zone Barrier. While the Crimson Cadre were imprisoned, the Genetic Council formed and alliance with Morgan, recovered the shrunken city of Attilan and forced the royal family back into their service. The Crimson Cadre were later rescued by Karnak and were part of the defensive trying to stop the Fantastic Four, Fantastic Force, the Sub-Mariner and Thor from reclaiming Atlantis and Attilan. Ultimately, Attilan was restored to its normal size and contained under a Negative Zone Barrier. Trapped outside, the Crimson Cadre were ordered to apprehend the Inhuman Royal Family by the Genetic Council's ruler Lord Arcadius, but failed. Eventually, the Inhuman Royal Family came back into power, and while celebrating the return of Crystal, the Crimson Cadre was enthralled by Maximus and his ally Fabian Cortez who tried to take down the royal family. The Cadre's ranks were increased with the addition of the renegade Inhumans Leonus, Falcona, and Stallior. The Cadre was easily dispatched and later Maximus and Cortez were quickly defeated. The Cadre was easily dispatched and later Maximus and Cortez were quickly defeated. The Crimson Cadre has not been seen since, and has possibly been disbanded.

atra.name: Atra
atra.origin: Circa 18,000 BC, Atra was the greatest human alchemist of the Deviant-controlled Lemuria. He and his circle of alchemists, with the help from the Serpent-Men, created the Serpent Crown. Unbeknownst to Atra, he was manipulated by the Deviants into creating the Crown, for the Deviant emperor Phraug to wear. By the time of the Great Cataclysm, the Deviants demanded he deliver the new weapon to them. In order to unlock the power of the Crown, Atra had to sacrifice to Set the blood of an innocent or an enemy. As his daughter Antilia urged him to reconsider his plan, Atra slew her, considering her to be both. Atra then attempted to use the Crown to destroy Phraug and take control of Lemuria, but Phraug was protected from the Crown's power by Set. Atra and Phraug fought over the Crown just as the Great Cataclysm occurred, destroying Lemuria but preserving their skeletons, both clutching the Crown.

atrea.name: Atrea
atrea.origin: A daughter of Thanos, Atrea who is unlike her siblings, possessing their support for Thanos' ideology, questions her father's motives "too many times". Her question ultimately cost her to have her left arm entirely stripped to a skeleton, but functional, as a punishment even when she tried to tell Thanos to stop. Sometime later, Atrea self-exiled herself from Acheron to her own paradise realm. When the Fantastic Four transported to Acheron in order for Thanos to possess the Cosmic Cube, Atrea knew that the team are in dire consequences. Feeling an affinity for the Thing, she whisked away Ben Grimm to her dimension. She then explained her reason to Ben that she should 'save' what was about to happen to Earth, its inhabitants and the universe from her father. Though Ben willingly wanted to regroup with his friends and stop Thanos, Atrea tried to convince him not to by revealing much about her father and his intentions with the Cosmic Cube. For example, she toured with him to the completely frozen world of Sidris displaying of Thanos' past ruthlessness. Finally, she then revealed that she intended to have Ben as her lover. Ben rejected Atrea's offer, angering her to display her power against him, intending to kill him. But, at this point Ben pointed out to her that she is no different from Thanos, forcing Atrea to guiltily relent. Atrea then promised to help Ben stop her father. After regrouping with Reed Richards, Atrea and the remaining Four travel to a changed Earth where she distracts her father allowing Ben and Reed to free Susan and Johnny Storm. Following this, Atrea witnessed Thanos' defeat and permanent death. Atrea also learned the origin of the Cosmic Cube. It was revealed that the paradox of Reed's manufactured Cube was that the item was, in reality, the original Cube that Thanos first discovered.

Conan unwittingly helped Prem, Atreah's sister, to bring his brother back to Mreead-zza to be sacrificed but once he arrived in that city where magic dominated, Conan was enchanted by making him believe he was Pram's betrothed, but when he saw that Atreah was about to be sacrificed he recovered from the spell by freeing Atreah and fighting against the deity who after being defeated by Conan plunged the inhabitants of Mreead-zzan into their ancient state of savages.

atrocity.first_appearance: Ghost Rider/Blaze: Spirits of Vengeance Vol 1 17
atrocity.origin: Atrocity was once a member of the Blood, an ancient group dedicated to fighting Zarathos' evil. Eventually, he turned his back on the Blood, and chose to worship Zarathos instead, becoming one of the Fallen. Atrocity may be as much as 20,000 years old. At one point, centuries or millennia ago, he fell in love with a South American woman named Xoc, but it ended badly, to Atrocity's eternal regret. He was killed by Blade in the South American temple of Foundry, using the Justiciar, a magic sword.

atropos.name: Atropos
atropos.origin: Atropos was the Olympian Goddess of Fate. As Aisa, she became one of the leaders of The Fist. When Dr. Alexi Cronos revealed to Spider-Man his affiliation to The Fist, Aisa remotely killed Cronos. She intervened between Captain America, Spider-Man, and Qweeg by dropping an automated tank in the middle of Times Square. While the heroes were distracted, Aisa escaped with Qweeg, recruiting him into Fist. She and Qweeg climbed the Rocky Mountains to recruit Glorianna. Aisa revealed herself and The Fist by broadcasting a message on television describing their anarchist ideology and belief that the United States of America had failed to live up to the ideals that it was founded on.

atsuko.name: Atsuko
atsuko.origin: In Japan during World War II, escaped American prisoners-of-war Logan and Ethan Warren came across Atsuko on a small farm in the woods. Warren (without evidence) thought Atsuko was an assassin working for the Emperor, and wanted to kill her. Logan and Warren fought, and Logan and Atsuko escaped together. Atsuko took Logan to a small house on the outskirts of the nearest city -- Hiroshima, where they made love. Warren found them, shot Logan in the head and then attempted to rape Atsuko. Atsuko fought back with a sword and was able to injure Warren, but eventually Warren stabbed her in the chest with a bayonet. At this point, Logan recovered from his injury, and Logan and Warren fought, each discovering the other was an indestructible mutant. Their evenly-matched fight was ended when the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. While they both survived, Atsuko was killed -- if she wasn't already dead from her wound. If Atsuko did die from the bombing, she was likely one of the many souls that contributed to the Everwraith, a being comprised of the souls of those who were killed during the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

att lass.name: Att-Lass
att lass.origin: Captain Atlas was one of the motherworld's most decorated soldiers. He first met Doctor Minerva when he was sent to Earth to retrieve her after she had signaled the Kree Empire that she had successfully unlocked her body's genetic potential. Minerva took a liking to Atlas and shared the Psyche-Magnitron process with him, causing him to transform into a superbeing who she considered to be her most eugenically ideal mate. As they were preparing to leave Earth, Atlas saw images of the Quantum Bands worn by Quasar and believed that they might be the legendary Power-Bands of Rinn. Posing as "Mr. Atlas" and "Dr. Minerva" from Xenotech, the two Kree attended the first international weapons exhibition to be held by A.I.M. and offered to pay them $100 million per bracelet if their technicians could acquire working replicas of the Quantum-Bands. A.I.M. sent M.O.D.A.M. to take them from Quasar but he defeated her. While in a New Mexico desert, Atlas and Minerva secretly watched as Quasar found and captured Halflife. Apparently obtaining the specific energy signature of the bands at that time, the two Kree were then able to track him to his home in Connecticut and, once he had fallen asleep, they used a synaptic disruptor to make sure he remained unconscious while they abducted him to their starcruiser. However, when Minerva's attempt to obtain the bands led to her trying to use a laser to cut off his left arm caused Quasar to awaken, he swiftly defeated both of them and ordered them to stay away from Earth in the future. Captain Atlas later worked with Doctor Minerva again during the Kree/Shi'ar conflict known on Earth as Operation: Galactic Storm and retrieved Captain Mar-Vell's Nega-Bands. Atlas wore the Nega-Bands for a short time, and used them to switch places with Rick Jones. Atlas battled the Avengers and the Shi'ar but when he discovered that the war had been instigated by the Supreme Intelligence in order to irradiate and jump start the evolution of the Kree, Atlas became disillusioned and claimed that he had activated his battle suit's self-destruct program in order to commit suicide. Doctor Minerva tried to stop his suicide but was seemingly vaporized along with him. thumb|left In actuality, this suicide was merely a tactic which Atlas and Minerva used to covertly escape from the Avengers by teleporting away under the cover of the blast. They ended up on a remote planet where they planned to become the parents of a race of Kree supermen. When the Silver Surfer happened to encounter them there, Minerva and Atlas attacked him but were easily defeated. Atlas again posed as a suicidal warrior, claiming that he had intended to kill himself on Hala but had lost his nerve and now felt that his honor demanded that he die because he had disgraced himself. Taken in by this ploy, the Surfer agreed to leave them there and keep the fact that they were still alive a secret. Years later, Captain Atlas set out to invade Earth on behalf of the Kree. To this end, he enlisted the services of Spymaster to steal multiple of Iron Man's armor to empower his army. Adopting the identity of Titanium Man, At-Lass joined the team of super villains gathered by Spymaster to complete his mission. The team carried out a heist on the Avengers Tower, and Spymaster used miniature teleporters to send numerous Iron Man suits to Atlas' ship, and teleported himself away as well. In order to tie loose ends, Titanium Man offered to teleport the rest of the villains to Spymaster's buyer, taking them with himself and revealing his true identity only after neutralizing them. After the villains freed themselves, Captain Atlas' ship was attacked by Iron Man, who had been alarmed of the theft. Spymaster's former allies joined forces with Iron Man to defend the Earth from Atlas' invasion attempt, and during the subsequent fight, Atlas was vaporized by Unicorn.

attican.name: Attican
attican.origin: Emperor Attican was the emperor of the Sinnarian Empire. As part of a game, the Grandmaster bet that the Sinnarian Empire could be destroyed by only five people. To make the game more interesting for himself, the Grandmaster manipulated Attican into obtaining the Bow of Gabriel. Attican used the bow to expand his empire by mutating the population of planets into monsters subservient to him. On the orders of the Grandmaster, the Black Order stole the Bow of Gabriel and used it to mutate everyone on Sinnar, including Attican.

attila the hun.name: Attila the Hun
attila the hun.origin: The origins of are lost to the ages; however, he was the ruler of the Hunnic Empire from 434 to 453 AD. During the battle of Chalons in 451 AD, Attila the Hun's attempts to invade Champagne-Ardenne were thwarted thanks to the assistance of 1940s time traveler Tommy Tyme, whose knowledge proved useful to Roman general Flavius Aëtius, who drove Attila and his minions back. At some point, Attila was summoned by the Martian Kara to the ruins of 30th century New York, where Kara intended to assemble an army of generals and soldiers from history to conquer the Solar System, including Achilles, Hector, Caesar, Alexander the Great, Hannibal, General Patton, Sversky, Allelo, Napoléon, Cromwell, and Lafayette. Instead, the assembled army turned against Kara and killed him, then warned Earth Government of the Martian threat, and offered to help as strategists. Humanity consequently conducted preemptive, genocidal strikes on the cities of Mars, though the time-displaced soldiers were of little use due to their lack of knowledge and understanding of the future surrounding them, and instead mostly watched and tried to learn. After Mars was wiped out, they were awarded a special medal voted by congress. Remaining there for another month to witness the future, they eventually said their goodbyes and faded away, returning to their respective eras, to the moment they had been taken, unbeknownst to all but them. Having realized the vastness of the universe, they all grasped the impossibility of conquering it, and all lost their appetite for war and conquest, explaining why none would conquer the Earth (though the statement seems dubious considering the lives and deaths of at least part of the time-displaced soldiers and generals). ===Afterlife=== After his death, his soul was sent to one of the many Hell Realms that exist in the afterlife, and became one of the most respected masters of torture under the command of a demon calling himself Satan. This demon made a pact with Adolf Hitler prior to the outbreak of World War II, and by the spring of 1943, "Satan" was not impressed with Hitler's progress following losses at the Russian front. Deciding it was time to replace Hitler with a more competent minion, Satan had his lover Madam Satan bring Attila with her to the surface world to take Hitler's place. Surprisingly, Hitler ceded control of the Nazis to Attila after Madam Satan showed the Fuhrer a gas that could turn people to stone. However, Attila did not get the chance to command his newly-acquired army, thanks to the intervention of the Destroyer. Although the Destroyer was initially turned into stone, he was restored to normal by exposure to heat, the one element that could reverse the transformation into stone. Battling with Attila, the Destroyer tossed the ancient warrior into a nearby fireplace. Contact with the flames shunted him back to Hell, and Madam Satan followed after him in defeat.

attuma.name: Attuma
attuma.species: Atlantean, later enhanced by Doctor Doom; formerly mutated by gamma radiation
attuma.origin: ===Early Life=== thumb|left|Attuma as a child The barbarian warlord known as Attuma was part of a sect of Homo mermanus, part of the Skarka Tribe that was exiled from the city of Atlantis some time ago, likely over their opposition of the royal ruling class. Prophecies spoke that a warrior would be born from the Skarka who would conquer Atlantis by force. Before Attuma was even born, his tribe was captured by the barbarian warrior Rorak. He had heard of the prophecy and sought to rule Atlantis by controlling the warrior's fate. Attuma was born during the battle, but his mother didn't survive. Attuma kept a clot of her blood from her heart. When Rorak saw this, he was so impressed that he spared the child's life. However, Attuma was put into slavery for years alongside all the women and children of his tribe. But while others grew weak and died, Attuma thrived working on the mines. The young Attuma soon grew strong, cunning and ruthless. Later as a youth, Attuma led his fellow Skarka to an uprising that slaughtered Rorak's minions while Rorak himself fled. During Attuma's teenage years, his father and chieftain of the Skarka Tribe - Attukar - began arranging for a treaty between the Atlantean Empire and the Skarka Tribe. Encountering the Atlantean prince Namor for the first time, the two initially became rivals for the affection of Lady Dorma but set aside their differences and began developing a burgeoning friendship for the sake of peace between their peoples. To encourage diplomatic relations, Attuma, Namor, and Dorma were sent to accompany the Swift Tide - an elite group of Atlantean warrior-women - on a mission to recover the Unforgotten Stone, an eldritch artifact created by the Great Old Ones. The mission ended in disaster when the Swift Tide were mutated into predatory monsters by the Unforgotten Stone's power; and their ensuing rampage - which resulted in the death of King Attukar and everyone else present at the Orreki Reefs - destroyed all hope of peace between the Skarka Tribe and the Atlantean Empire, and friendship between Attuma and Namor. The Skarka Tribe then settled in an area of the ocean referred to as the "Murky Depths". This society, too, prophesied that one of their own would one day overthrow the throne of Atlantis. From that moment on, Attuma was told by his people that he would be that person and since then he has lived by the sword. Through the years, Attuma grew to be the most powerful of his people, his ruthlessness cementing him as their leader. Attuma transformed the Skarka Tribe into an army of thousands from the Murky Depths, leading his tribe on a path of violent conquest. At some point in his adult life, Attuma sired a number of children. His first born was Andromeda with Lady Gelva, an Atlantean aristocrat allied with Attuma whom the warlord personally despised. Andromeda shamed Attuma for being female. Nonetheless, Attuma had the girl trained to be a warrior as though she were Attuma's son. Andromeda sought to prove herself by joining the Atlantean Army that opposed her father. The fate of his other children are unknown, however its possible they were estranged from their father in much the same way Andromeda was. ===Bid for Conquest=== thumb|250px|left|Attuma's original armor In the modern age, Attuma decided to meet his supposed destiny and made a bit to conquer Atlantis, which at the time was ruled by the Namor - now known as the Sub-Mariner. Although Attuma's armies were many, they were no match for the army of Atlantis. However, the battle soon turned to Attuma's favor when Namor spurred the love of Lady Dorma. Angry at the Sub-Mariner for rejecting her love, she assisted Attuma in breaching the defenses of Atlantis in exchange for ruling at his side. Dorma realized the grave error she made when Attuma rejected her after they battled through the defenses. Seeking aid, Dorma went to the surface world and enlisted Namor's sometime enemies the Fantastic Four, convincing them that Attuma would be an even greater threat to the surface world than Namor ever could be. Operating in secret, the Fantastic Four routed Attuma's armies and the Invisible Girl utilized her powers to assist Namor in combat against Attuma. Unaware of this aid, Namor defeated Attuma in one-on-one combat and defeated him. With his armies crushed, Attuma was summarily ejected from Atlantis, the first of many embarrassing defeats. Recovering from this defeat, Attuma decided to set his sights to conquer the surface world instead. Needing to study humans, Attuma and his forces constructed a base on a deserted island. They then captured a commercial airliner to study the people on board. Seeing a woman among their numbers, Attuma decided to begin his study with her. This proved to be Attuma's undoing as the woman in question was Janet van Dyne, secretly the size changing hero known as the Wasp. fields.history: ===Early Life=== thumb|left|Attuma as a child The barbarian warlord known as Attuma was part of a sect of Homo mermanus, part of the Skarka Tribe that was exiled from the city of Atlantis some time ago, likely over their opposition of the royal ruling class. Prophecies spoke that a warrior would be born from the Skarka who would conquer Atlantis by force. Before Attuma was even born, his tribe was captured by the barbarian warrior Rorak. He had heard of the prophecy and sought to rule Atlantis by controlling the warrior's fate. Attuma was born during the battle, but his mother didn't survive. Attuma kept a clot of her blood from her heart. When Rorak saw this, he was so impressed that he spared the child's life. However, Attuma was put into slavery for years alongside all the women and children of his tribe. But while others grew weak and died, Attuma thrived working on the mines. The young Attuma soon grew strong, cunning and ruthless. Later as a youth, Attuma led his fellow Skarka to an uprising that slaughtered Rorak's minions while Rorak himself fled. During Attuma's teenage years, his father and chieftain of the Skarka Tribe - Attukar - began arranging for a treaty between the Atlantean Empire and the Skarka Tribe. Encountering the Atlantean prince Namor for the first time, the two initially became rivals for the affection of Lady Dorma but set aside their differences and began developing a burgeoning friendship for the sake of peace between their peoples. To encourage diplomatic relations, Attuma, Namor, and Dorma were sent to accompany the Swift Tide - an elite group of Atlantean warrior-women - on a mission to recover the Unforgotten Stone, an eldritch artifact created by the Great Old Ones. The mission ended in disaster when the Swift Tide were mutated into predatory monsters by the Unforgotten Stone's power; and their ensuing rampage - which resulted in the death of King Attukar and everyone else present at the Orreki Reefs - destroyed all hope of peace between the Skarka Tribe and the Atlantean Empire, and friendship between Attuma and Namor. The Skarka Tribe then settled in an area of the ocean referred to as the "Murky Depths". This society, too, prophesied that one of their own would one day overthrow the throne of Atlantis. From that moment on, Attuma was told by his people that he would be that person and since then he has lived by the sword. Through the years, Attuma grew to be the most powerful of his people, his ruthlessness cementing him as their leader. Attuma transformed the Skarka Tribe into an army of thousands from the Murky Depths, leading his tribe on a path of violent conquest. At some point in his adult life, Attuma sired a number of children. His first born was Andromeda with Lady Gelva, an Atlantean aristocrat allied with Attuma whom the warlord personally despised. Andromeda shamed Attuma for being female. Nonetheless, Attuma had the girl trained to be a warrior as though she were Attuma's son. Andromeda sought to prove herself by joining the Atlantean Army that opposed her father. The fate of his other children are unknown, however its possible they were estranged from their father in much the same way Andromeda was. ===Bid for Conquest=== thumb|250px|left|Attuma's original armor In the modern age, Attuma decided to meet his supposed destiny and made a bit to conquer Atlantis, which at the time was ruled by the Namor - now known as the Sub-Mariner. Although Attuma's armies were many, they were no match for the army of Atlantis. However, the battle soon turned to Attuma's favor when Namor spurred the love of Lady Dorma. Angry at the Sub-Mariner for rejecting her love, she assisted Attuma in breaching the defenses of Atlantis in exchange for ruling at his side. Dorma realized the grave error she made when Attuma rejected her after they battled through the defenses. Seeking aid, Dorma went to the surface world and enlisted Namor's sometime enemies the Fantastic Four, convincing them that Attuma would be an even greater threat to the surface world than Namor ever could be. Operating in secret, the Fantastic Four routed Attuma's armies and the Invisible Girl utilized her powers to assist Namor in combat against Attuma. Unaware of this aid, Namor defeated Attuma in one-on-one combat and defeated him. With his armies crushed, Attuma was summarily ejected from Atlantis, the first of many embarrassing defeats. Recovering from this defeat, Attuma decided to set his sights to conquer the surface world instead. Needing to study humans, Attuma and his forces constructed a base on a deserted island. They then captured a commercial airliner to study the people on board. Seeing a woman among their numbers, Attuma decided to begin his study with her. This proved to be Attuma's undoing as the woman in question was Janet van Dyne, secretly the size changing hero known as the Wasp. attumacht.name: Attumacht
attumacht.origin: Attumacht was an Atlantean warlord and the leader of the barbarian Skar-Ka, circa 9,000 BC. The Skar-Ka warred against many villages, including the Sera Thet tribe, which lived in the village of Sera Thet and were led by Orelem. According to Orelem, the Skar-Ka had been raping and pillaging the Sera Thet for ages. The Sera Thet were joined by time-displaced "Brighthair" (Namorita/Kymaera), who tried to help them without endangering the timestream. Kymaera spied on the Skar-Ka, and discovered that their warlord Attumacht had invented a weapon combining a club and an axe, which ensured technological superiority over the Sera Thet. He invented and made manufacture a new type of weapon that would give him a technological edge on the Sera Thet. When one of his own warriors suggested it might be better to instead work with the Sera Thet, Attumacht executed him. Menawhile, Kymaera decided to train them, diverted tools into weapons, in order for them to repel the Skar-Ka, only to discover horrified that Orelem intended to wipe out the Skar-Ka entirely. Kymaera broke out the fighting, and forced Orelem and Attumacht to consider their respective strengths and weaknesses, and realize their mutual interest self-preservation by working together, bringing them together. ===Legacy=== The Skarka endured into the Modern Age, and Attumacht was descended by the barbarian Attuma, and Andromeda. Hellfall Deep, the ancestral lands of the Skarka Tribe, was located within the Attumacht Trench.

atul.origin: Atul and Ingu were the two Watchers who took Uatu from his Citadel and transported him to the Watchers' World to put him on trial after Uatu had declared himself unworthy. They did not notice that they were followed by Captain Marvel, and as soon as they noticed his presence and warned him that no mortal was allowed to go to their planet and despite the request of Mar-Vell who wanted to testify in Uatu's defense the two decided to put him in stasis for fear that if they sent him away he might follow them.

atul pandya.name: Atul Pandya
atul pandya.origin: Atul Pandya was a scientist that was commandeered to create a bio-engineered weapons created from conglomerated mutant genes for an Indian terrorist organization. He was the target for a mission given to the X-Men by Weapon X to acquire his services for S.H.I.E.L.D.. Unfortunately, the higher officials of the organization decided to change to orders of the mission to have Atul terminated. Despite pleading for his life, he was killed by Jean Grey after she was forced to choose between killing Atul or letting Cyclops be killed for insubordination.
