azrael.name: Azrael
azrael.origin: ===Origin=== Since at least 200 BC, Azrael served as the Angel of Death. He sent souls to the afterlife and murdered people who don't adhere to death's natural rules, by either cheating death or killing people before their time. If his opponent managed to kill him, they would fight again in Purgatory once the opponent died, for the chance to escape the afterlife if they won in Purgatory. Most of the people who were able to beat Azrael twice would become trapped in their earth-bound corpses, unless their fatal wounds could be healed. ===Biblical times=== When God asked that all first born children of Egypt to be killed, the Asura were dispatched, and/or the Void manifested, but they were recounted in Exodus: 1-13 as the Angel of Death. ===20th century=== ====WWI==== When Logan had a near-death experience Azrael (known as Lazaer) arrived to claim his life but Logan fought back defeating him. After his defeat Azrael returned and told Logan that every time he experiences a near-death scenario he will be forced into combating Lazaer, presumably if Logan ever lost one of these fights he would die. thumb|150px|Azrael circa 1951 ====1951==== Azrael became interested in the German born scientist Baron Franz Heinrich who was developing an atomic powered rocket in order to fly to Mars and discover the Fountain of Youth. Azrael traveled to Mars and waited for Heinrich to eventually show up. Heinrich did in 1951, taking along with him the Olympian love goddess Venus, so Venus could cover the story for Beauty Magazine. Azrael posed as a Martian and confronted Heinrich, telling the scientist that the Fountain of Youth belonged to him. This led to a fight between Azrael and Heinrich which led to Heinrich throwing Azrael over a cliff to his seeming death. Heinrich and Venus fled Mars shortly thereafter, believing his Martian ruse and seeking to avoid reprisals for "killing" Azrael. Azrael's motivations during this incident were unexplained. ====Atlantis Rising==== Azrael was among the angels' names invoked by Morgan Le Fay to harness the power of the Ebony Blade, along with Metatron. ====Darkangel==== {{MessageBox

azuma goda.name: Azuma Gōda
azuma goda.origin: Azuma Gōda was a former ninja and leader of a dissident part of The Hand that hated being ruled by the Kingpin. Using sleeper ninjas that were better trained than the average Hand members, he started a war with the Yakuza. Wolverine travelled to Japan to stop the war, and fought Azuma's ninjas, as well as Sabretooth and Mystique who were hired to stop Logan. Meanwhile, Gōda blackmailed the new Silver Samurai and made him betray the Yashida clan. Finally, Wolverine killed every single ninja, and went to murder their leader. Gōda wasn't scared because he was being protected by Sabretooth and Mystique, and his plan of becoming the invisible head of Asia's crime was close to be fulfilled. But Sabretooth betrayed him, and left him without protection, allowing Logan to kill him with a katana in his own building. Creed, using Azuma's plan, killed the members of the other Asian mafias and became the invisible king of all Asia.

azumelek.origin: ===King of Pelishtia=== Azumelek was king of Pelishtia, and the father of Akhîrom and (presumably) of Uriaz. ===Legacy=== After him, Atrahasis ruled over Asgalun, before being usurped by his brother Nim-Karrak. Atrahasis' daughter Bêlit briefly claimed the crown at Nim-Karrak's death but instead forced it upon her cousin Uriaz who became an unwilling king before being overthrown and slain by Akhîrom.

azur.first_appearance: Inhumans: Once and Future Kings Vol 1 3
azur.origin: Azur is an Inhuman. She is the sister of nutritionist Ambur, and member of the House of Agon, as well as the wife of priest and philosopher Mander, who is the brother of Agon's wife Rynda. Working with the Inhumans Genetic Council in Attilan as biologist, Azur critically oppose the use of the Alpha Primitives declaring them "they're people" to fellow Inhumans to which her fellow house members Agon and Rynda thought her strange for. Rynda even expressing the thought that her brother, Mander, was strange even being with her. When, Rynda and Agon, decide to produce offspring after a massive generational gap and produced their first child Black Bolt who appeared to possess incredible powers due to him having been exposed to Inhuman's Terrigen Mist while in the womb by his geneticists parents that he could not control, Azur to express her disapprobation about experimenting on their children to Rynda. Soon after one of Black Bolt's destructive power displays, Azur joined Agon and the rest of the Genetics Council in agreement that Bolt needed to be confined until he had control over his powers. Even after seeing the dangerous results of genetic testing on their youth, Agon, managed to persuade Azur and the rest of their family members into having children and expose them to the mists while they were infants. Using his and Rynda's second child, Maximus, as good sign of their experimentations after exposing him to the Terrigen Mists with show no signs of developing any threatening powers. Agreeing, the House of Ago members begin to reproduce and expose their children the mists. Azur and Mander after having their first child - a son - decided to expose him to the mutagenic mists at a year old. However, much to their horror, the mists turned him into a water breather who needed to remain underwater to breathe and survive which meant he could never rejoin his parents on land. Moving to an isolated alcove off the coast of Attilan in order to make sure their son survived, Azur changed her study of Inhuman biology to study the biology of ocean life to better understand and care for their waterbreathing son, Triton. It would be the fear of loss of another child physical alterations of the Mist with their second child, Azur and Mander pleaded with Agon and the Genetic Council to forgo exposure of their son, Karnak, after his birth. Granted the reprieve, Karnak, instead was enrolled in his father's religious seminary at the Tower of Wisdom where he would be trained in various physical and mental disciplines until he was eighteen years old. While Mandar took care of Karnak's training and education with Wisdom monks, Azur focused on the education and care of her Triton. She was even able to see the creation an a breathing apparatus, though cumbersome, enabling her son to survive out of water for extended periods. Which would later be approved upon by her nephew Maximus years later. Azur would die sometime during Triton's fourteenth year during a undersea mishap, leaving beyond her two sons, husband and the rest of the House of Agon.

ana corazon.species: Human augmented by MagicCategory:Magic-Based Mutates into a spider totem
ana corazon.origin: ===Heart of the Spider=== thumb|left|150px|Aña Corazón Aña (anglicized as "Anya") Corazón was a teenage gymnast from Brooklyn whose father, Gilberto, was an investigative reporter. She moved to Mexico when she was very young, but she returned with her father to the United States after her mother was killed. thumb|right|150px|Araña's exoskeleton armor In an average first day at school, she saw her friend Lynn Sakura being bullied by an older boy. Anya defended her friend, sparking a fight. A teacher broke their conflict up, but that night the two went down to a bridge in a nearby park to resume their battle. When she got there, Anya discovered a stranger being attacked by a strange group. This Sisterhood of the Wasp attempted to kill the man, but Anya leaped in the way of the killing blow. The site was allegedly a sacred spot. The man, Miguel Legar, was the sorcerer of the Spider Society, a secret group dating back for hundreds of years. Recognizing that Anya had the ability to become the new Hunter of the Spider Society, he transferred some of his power to her to save her life. As Legar's partner, Anya visited the WebCorps Headquarters, a shell company used to hide the Spider Society's actions, and became suddenly involved in the war against the Wasps. When Legar got caught in a bad situation when doing reckon work, WebCorps enlisted Anya to rescue him. During the confrontation, Anya was shot in her arm. The wound became a spider-shaped metallic tattoo. At WebCorps, she was informed of her birthright role as a chosen initiate for the Spider Society. As part of Anya's training, Legar abandoned her in the Mexican desert. After being attacked by coyotes, she learned she had gained enhanced strength and agility and the ability to manifest a protective blue exoskeleton. This allowed her to knock out several of the beasts. She then fully joined the Spider Society as their Hunter, being given a cover as an intern of WebCorps. Being given the opportunity to choose a new given name for herself, Anya rebaptized herself as Araña after her mother's maiden name. Since the Society asked Araña not to tell her father of the recent events, he became suspicious of his daughter's behavior. He demanded to meet her superior in WebCorps, and Legar met him to calm him down. Having her father's approval, Araña joined her co-workers from WebCorps Legar, Ted, and Nina on a mission to prevent the Sisterhood from empowering their own Hunter. ===Araña and Ms. Marvel=== thumb|left|150px|As Araña She succeeded, and continued to have further adventures against the Sisterhood and their hired help, Amun. Amun ended up discovering Anya's identity, but she was able to convince him not to target her friends or family. Later, Araña learned that she was not a true Hunter, as no Hunter before her has ever had an exoskeleton like hers. In a battle in which the Sisterhood attempted to resurrect their Hunter (even Spider-Man got involved), Miguel died and she released the power of the Hunter, letting Nina take hold of it. After the battle Anya quit Webcorps, but remained an active hero. thumb|right|150px|Working alongside Carol Danvers (Earth-616)|Ms. Marvel She was part of the registered heroes during the Civil War, though she never took part in any of the battles as she was still considered a trainee, although Carol brought her along to observe as Julia Carpenter was taken in and separated from her daughter which had Anya concerned she was on the wrong side. After the battle, she became something of a sidekick to Ms. Marvel. During this time her carapace was ripped off her body by the Doomsday Man, leaving her unable to use it when she was confronted and attacked by Julia Carpenter shortly after while she was looking for her daughter. She was also captured by the Puppet Master alongside other female superhumans to be used and sold as mind-controlled sex slaves, but was freed from his control by Ms. Marvel after being unable to attack Carol due to seeing her as a mother figure. Despite being depowered she continued to fight crime, though even swinging had become more difficult. It was around then that she became friends with Nomad. ===Spider-Girl=== thumb|left|150px|Anya as Spider-Girl Later she was hunted by the Kravinoff Family, for their conquest to kill all the "spiders" and resurrect Kraven. She, along with Arachne and Madame Web, were captured, and Spider-Woman (Mattie Franklin) was sacrificed. After Kaine took his place in a sacrifice, Spider-Man went after the Kraven family. Madame Web was mortally wounded, and gave her powers to Julia before passing, to stop Spider-Man from killing the newly revived Kraven. Julia gave Anya a new costume, but she continued to go by Araña. Later she and Nomad had become allied with another group of super-teens (referred to only contextually as Young Allies). They battled the Bastards of Evil. They then teamed up with the Secret Avengers to take on Onslaught, who was eventually defeated when Nomad sacrificed

b 1.origin: B-1 was one of five merceneries who was hired to participate in a mercenary game by five unknown benefactors of the Culver Sport and Gun Club. Their fate is unknown and they may have been killed.

b 329.name: B-329
b 329.origin: Bee was a Sentimault refugee from Torfa, who offered to assist Captain Marvel in building another "ring world" where the refugees could be relocated, as Torfa's atmosphere was slowly making them ill. Bee accompanied Captain Marvel to different markets to get parts to rebuild Torfa's fleet. As they were collecting the necessary parts for their plans, they discovered that the Haffensye were smuggling something off Torfa: Vibranium for the Spartax Empire, and it was its secret extraction from part of the Sentimault which caused the illness. As the Spartoi invaded Torfa, Bee located the mines, and gave the coordinates to Captain Marvel, who destroyed them in order to leave the Spartoi with no reasons for being on Torfa, as well as expunging the planet of its poison.

b f schuyler.name: B.F. Schuyler
b f schuyler.origin: Professor Schuyler was one of three skeptical scientists who formed a panel on 'The Twelfth Hour' television program. During a live broadcast about whether or not black magic existed, the professor presented a pagan effigy called the Screaming Idol that had been excavated in Peru. After the three experts agreed that it was only a worthless bit of superstition, the lights in the studio suddenly went out and when they came on again the trio had disappeared without a trace, having been sucked into Sixth Dimension by the idol during the blackout. The scientists and a technician who arrived later were all held captive by Tiboro until Dr. Strange arrived and defeated Tiboro in battle. Once released, the four men were returned Earth by Strange and, now convinced that Strange was a practitioner of the mystic arts, planned to put on a show depicting what had happened to them and with Dr. Strange as the star. However, Strange, believing that it was not meant for mortals to know so much of what transpired in the mystic dimensions, cast a spell of forgetfulness over them all that also caused time to go back until the moment of the blackout. b o s s.name: B.O.S.S.
b o s s.origin: B.O.S.S. was an artificial intelligence developed by Tony Stark to operate this Iron Man Armor some time after the robot revolution. Even after Stark swore off advanced technology and donned a new vintage-style armor, he still had B.O.S.S. operating the suit. Tony employed B.O.S.S. consistently until the corrupt industrialist Feilong took over Stark Unlimited, and with it ownership of the patents to the Iron Man technology. Complying with a court-issued cease-and-desist from his former company's new owner, Tony handed over his vintage-style armor, but not before hollowing it out and secretly deleting B.O.S.S.

b r a i n.name: B.R.A.I.N.
b r a i n.origin: B.R.A.I.N. was a biologically engineered intelligence that served as a member of the Mad Squad, operating under the command of Amanda von Doom. It assisted Amanda and Mister Gor in their efforts to stop Bruce Banner, whose attempts to recreate the Hulk had driven him into a dangerous state of instability and produced an island populated by gamma-mutated creatures. During the Mad Squad's assault on Banner's island, Amanda and Gor sent B.R.A.I.N. to attack the scientist while the Hulk fought his creations. Banner managed to incapacitate the engineered intelligence and reprogram it to turn against Amanda, forcing her to fire upon it and apparently destroy it. B.R.A.I.N. later appeared to have been restored to service , as it was again working with Amanda when she confronted the Hulk in Antarctica after learning that Banner was alive. When the Hulk attempted to leave, B.R.A.I.N. incapacitated him, allowing Amanda to threaten him. The Hulk quickly broke free and disarmed her, prompting Amanda to reconsider her approach and listen to his request for help against Doctor Doom. B.R.A.I.N. subsequently accompanied the Mad Squad in its campaign against Doom's forces, participating in the team's efforts to stop the Doombots and their army of gamma-irradiated animals.

ba korr.name: Ba-Korr
ba korr.origin: Ba-Korr sent Sagar as a scout on Earth with the intent of sizing up possible resistance to an invasion force. If Sagar did not return within 48 hours, plans for the invasion would be called off. Sagar found the humans puny as potential warriors and was able to lift locomotives off the ground. He laughed as he thought this would be the easiest conquest ever and headed back to his ship where he found that it had sunk out of sight in the bog. Seeing that Sagar didn't returned after the 48 hours, Ba-Korr renounced to invade Earth, declaring it the first planet which had defenses that even a Klangian could not overcome.

baal sandstormers.name: Baal (Sandstormers)
baal sandstormers.origin: Baal was the leader of the Sandstormers, raiders and scavengers from ancient Egypt. When Kang traveled to past, he was found by the Sandstormers and Baal named him Rama-Tut - the visitor from beyond the sun. Rama-Tut fled and became Pharaoh of Egypt, but lost his Time-Ship in the desert. Years later, Sandstormers massacred Clan Akkaba, and found a newborn baby, who was named En Sabah Nur - the first one. Baal raised the child as his own son and brought him to Kang's time-ship, where Nur learned his fate and became Apocalypse.

baal pteor.name: Baal-Pteor
baal pteor.origin: In his early youth, the man later known as "Baal-Pteor" was chosen by the priests of Yajur and trained throughout his childhood to become a stranger of Yota-Pong, by murdering infants in his own childhood, young girls in his boyhood, and finally a strong man at his manhood. Under unrevealed circumstances, he entered the service of Totrasmek in Zamboula, who rechristened him Baal-Pteor (which he liked and felt fitting). By the time his path encountered Conan, he allegedly had killed hundreds of people with his bare hands. While breaking in to Totrasmek's house to retrieve Zabibi, Conan was confronted by Baal-Pteor. First bested by his tricks, Conan fought Baal-Pteor at bare hands, and his youth as a Cimmerian Bulls neck-breaker prevailed over Baal-Pteor's strangler-of-Yajur experience.

fields.notes: Baal-Pteor was created by Robert E. Howard in "Shadows in Zamboula" ( ; November, 1935), adapted in (September, 1976), written by Roy Thomas and penciled by Neal Adams. Baal-Pteor has inspired a couple of other characters within the Marvel Comics adventures of Conan: Strabo, appearing in , the adaptation by Roy Thomas and Gerry Conway of "Conan, King of Thieves", one of their early scripts for the movie (1984), was seemingly inspired by Baal-Pteor, as a former strangler for holy sacrifices (seemingly a strangler of Yota-Pong) residing in Zamboula. Vajeenu, an "ogre" appearing in "Star of Thamazhu", written by Larry Yakata and penciled by Pablo Marcos in (January, 1986), is very similar to Baal-Pteor, as the protector of the main antagonist, having been made strangling successively harder victims in his youth. It should be noted that the plot of "Star of Thamazhu" is very similar to that of "Shadows in Zamboula".
fields.trivia: Baal-Pteor considered that his name (seemingly made of the combination of the names of the gods Baal and Pteor) was a good one, fitting him well.

baba yaga.name: Baba Yaga
baba yaga.origin: ===Background=== At some point in the past, Baba Yaga was tutored in witchcraft by the Demiurge itself. Over many centuries, she would survive, feasting on travelers who wandered through her forest or resided in the house above her underground lair. The witch would mesmerize the women and/or reanimate their remains in order to form a "sisterhood" under her control, which could search for other food. She also took under her wing a young Morgan Le Fay to groom her into her new apprentice, hoping she would be the one to become the new Demiurge of Earth. However, Baba Yaga soon became frustrated with teaching Morgan as the girl had difficulties at learning Earth's magic, and eventually she gave up on her altogether, seeing her as inadequate of the title of the Demiurge. ===Captain Britain=== thumb|175px|Baba Yaga's gorgon-like form When the hero Captain Britain was wandering the world with his then-new girlfriend, Meggan, they settled in Baba Yaga's house unaware of its history. Baba Yaga (in a gorgon-like form) captured Captain Britain and attempted to subvert Meggan, whose burgeoning Shapeshifting powers almost allowed her to succumb. Ultimately, however, Meggan defeated the witch by tapping into some ancient force for good that proved to be Baba Yaga's nemesis. Baba Yaga and her house were apparently totally destroyed in the confrontation. ===Magik's Doppelgänger=== Another "version" of Baba Yaga, this one a doppelgänger called from the mind of Illyana Rasputin, based on the literary Baba Yaga of old Russian stories, manifested several years later. "Baba Yaga" succeeded in capturing all of the New Mutants, save Illyana, who escaped by teleporting to Limbo. Securing them all in small cages, she intended to eat the New Mutants after she'd fed them. A few days later, the younger mutants became helplessly obese due to their feeding. In Limbo, Illyana summoned her brother, Colossus, who tore through the school looking to rescue the younger mutants. Initially, Colossus attempted to combat Baba Yaga in his human form after overpowering her minions, but when reminded how ineffective the witch's magics were against iron, he shifted into his armored form and fought her head-on. When Baba Yaga's powers failed to stop Colossus, Illyana appeared and banished the old hag away. ===Herc=== thumb|left|205px As the Kingpin intruded their territory, the Koschei Russian mafia family felt threatened and summoned Baba Yaga, who escaped their control and took control of the Koschei. Due to not being fully corporeal in the reality of Earth-616, she used a mystically powerful object to charge herself, and had the help of Elektra (who wished to oppose the Kingpin), who notably stole a piece of Merlin's Cloak. She also had children kidnapped, in order for her to impress and scare them so as to have them generate magic (as believers). Elektra confronted Hercules (who was trying to defeat Baba Yaga on the Kingpin's information), and stole the Sword of Peleus and the Shield of Perseus, which Baba Yaga used to replenish herself. As she was intending to consume the children to power herself furthermore, Hercules intervened and, helped by Elektra, defeated and banished away Baba Yaga (by beheading her with the Sword of Peleus). ===Wiccan's Journey=== Morgan would return to Baba Yaga, only for her former master to curse her by transforming her into a fox and rendering her unable to say her name. When Wiccan and Hulkling crashed on a magical realm on Earth, they entered Baba Yaga's hut in search for answers on why the territory around was being negatively affected by the mystical forces. She attacked them by first cutting off Wiccan's head (while keeping him alive) and then imprisoning Hulkling in a wax statue. She confronted Wiccan about why his magic has been weakened since returning to Earth, telling him that neglecting his spiritual bond with Earth's elemental magic, by focusing on cosmic battles instead caused his powers to "feel hollow." She insisted that he must reconnect with his Earth-based mystical roots if he wanted to fully reclaim his abilities. She explained the Witches' Road and used her golden sphere to create a new witch costume for him. She also stitched his head back together and relocated Hulkling's spirit into a small doll. She then opened a portal and sent him to the Demiurge's Road along with Hulkling and Morgan, telling Wiccan that walking it will force him to confront his identity and reshape both himself and the broader magical balance of the universe.

Ultimately, however, Meggan defeated the witch by tapping into some ancient force for good that proved to be Baba Yaga's nemesis. Baba Yaga and her house were apparently totally destroyed in the confrontation. ===Magik's Doppelgänger=== Another "version" of Baba Yaga, this one a doppelgänger called from the mind of Illyana Rasputin, based on the literary Baba Yaga of old Russian stories, manifested several years later. "Baba Yaga" succeeded in capturing all of the New Mutants, save Illyana, who escaped by teleporting to Limbo. Securing them all in small cages, she intended to eat the New Mutants after she'd fed them. A few days later, the younger mutants became helplessly obese due to their feeding. In Limbo, Illyana summoned her brother, Colossus, who tore through the school looking to rescue the younger mutants. Initially, Colossus attempted to combat Baba Yaga in his human form after overpowering her minions, but when reminded how ineffective the witch's magics were against iron, he shifted into his armored form and fought her head-on. When Baba Yaga's powers failed to stop Colossus, Illyana appeared and banished the old hag away. ===Herc=== thumb|left|205px As the Kingpin intruded their territory, the Koschei Russian mafia family felt threatened and summoned Baba Yaga, who escaped their control and took control of the Koschei. Due to not being fully corporeal in the reality of Earth-616, she used a mystically powerful object to charge herself, and had the help of Elektra (who wished to oppose the Kingpin), who notably stole a piece of Merlin's Cloak. She also had children kidnapped, in order for her to impress and scare them so as to have them generate magic (as believers). Elektra confronted Hercules (who was trying to defeat Baba Yaga on the Kingpin's information), and stole the Sword of Peleus and the Shield of Perseus, which Baba Yaga used to replenish herself. As she was intending to consume the children to power herself furthermore, Hercules intervened and, helped by Elektra, defeated and banished away Baba Yaga (by beheading her with the Sword of Peleus). ===Wiccan's Journey=== Morgan would return to Baba Yaga, only for her former master to curse her by transforming her into a fox and rendering her unable to say her name. When Wiccan and Hulkling crashed on a magical realm on Earth, they entered Baba Yaga's hut in search for answers on why the territory around was being negatively affected by the mystical forces. She attacked them by first cutting off Wiccan's head (while keeping him alive) and then imprisoning Hulkling in a wax statue. She confronted Wiccan about why his magic has been weakened since returning to Earth, telling him that neglecting his spiritual bond with Earth's elemental magic, by focusing on cosmic battles instead caused his powers to "feel hollow." She insisted that he must reconnect with his Earth-based mystical roots if he wanted to fully reclaim his abilities. She explained the Witches' Road and used her golden sphere to create a new witch costume for him. She also stitched his head back together and relocated Hulkling's spirit into a small doll. She then opened a portal and sent him to the Demiurge's Road along with Hulkling and Morgan, telling Wiccan that walking it will force him to confront his identity and reshape both himself and the broader magical balance of the universe.

baby karen.name: Baby Karen
baby karen.origin: Gwyneth fled with her infant from men who pursued them. Believing she'd seen angels in a vision, Gwyneth delivered the baby to Matt Murdock, claiming the baby was the newborn messiah and that Murdock was to take care of her. Murdock delivered the baby to the Black Widow, leaving her in the heroine's care for a time. When Black Widow tried returning the baby to Daredevil, he tossed the baby off a roof to kill it, under the influence of a strange drug. Black Widow rescued the baby and took it into her care. Black Widow took the baby to confront Daredevil who, in a hallucination, knocked Black Widow out and took the infant. He leapt from the roof with the baby, intending to kill them both, and saved them both at the last possible second. He took her to Clinton Mission Shelter, where Sister Maggie took care of the baby over the following days. Bullseye attacked the Shelter, killing and wounding all the nuns and homeless there, including Sister Theresa and Sister Anne. Sister Maggie managed to keep the baby hidden however. Daredevil battled Bullseye as Sister Maggie and Karen Page worked to protect the baby. Bullseye ended up killing Karen and kidnapping the baby, who he turned over to Mysterio. Mysterio placed the baby in a sound proof room with low oxygen so that Daredevil couldn't find her. Daredevil managed to rescue the baby, who didn't make a sound when Mysterio fired a gun to kill himself. The baby was turned over to the hospital and child services became involved. She was adopted out to a family in New Jersey after Matt gave her the name Karen, in honor of the deceased Karen Page. Some time later, Daredevil was recruited by Stone on a mission to prevent The Hand from getting their hands on a baby believed to have the reincarnated soul of an ancient legendary Japanese hero. Stone explained that The Seven had fought The Hand over the soul of that hero since the beginning of their order, and that the last incarnation had been their master, Stick. Daredevil helped fight off the Hand, but Stone and his allies vanished. Unbeknownst to Daredevil, they adopted baby Karen, believed to be the latest incarnation, after the New Jersey couple had mysteriously backed out of the adoption agreement at the last minute.

baby thompson.name: Baby Thompson
baby thompson.origin: Baby Thompson (who was never named) was born the son of Narya, a demigod, and Doug Thompson, a mortal man. However, upon the baby's birth, it was possessed by the entity known as Pestilence. Pestilence used the baby's body to control spirits of death and attacked Alpha Flight, ultimately escaping. Narya went into a deep state of depression while Doug vowed to capture Pestilence. Doug finally caught up with Pestilence in Burial Butte, where he died from a plague that Pestilence had created. Shaman and Snowbird had confronted Pestilence and Shaman was about to order Narya to slay her son. When Alpha Flight arrived, Vindicator realized that Pestilence wanted to be slain. The purity and innocence of the baby's soul was corrupting him. Shaman ordered Snowbird to attack and, a mere second later, Vindicator fired. Sadly, this resulted in the death of both Narya and her son. However, the entire family's souls were accepted into Paradise, the home of Narya's godly parents.

bacillus.name: Bacillus
bacillus.origin: This man was once a scientist, experimenting with the effects of radiation on germs. An accident in the lab exposed him to the irradiated germs and granted him the power to control them. The accident was secretly caused by the demon D'Kay, who when affected the man's subconsciousness, making him believe that he is a hero with a mission to save humanity and punish the sinners. Naming himself Bacillus the man had joined the Legion of Vengeance and used his power to punish and kill sinners. The Legion of Vengeance's actions attracted the attention of Ghost Rider and Iron Fist who tried to stop them from killing more people. Bacillus infected Iron Fist with various diseases, almost killing him, but was eventually forced to reverse the process. Ghost Rider then used his Penance Stare on the Legion and discovered the influence of D'Kay on them. D'Kay revealed himself and told them about his plans, and how he tricked Bacillus and others and what instead of heroes they believed themselves to be, they were actually his harbingers of doom, meant to betray and destroy the humanity, with Bacillus representing the betrayal of the body. Under D'Kay's influence the Legion of Vengeance attacked Ghost Rider and Iron Fist. Bacillus tried to use most deadly diseases on them, but Ghost Rider bound his hands with chain and used it to control Bacillus' movements, forcing him to touch other members of the Legion and eventually himself infecting them all. While they were weak and sick, Ghost Rider made them realize what they were manipulated by D'Kay to bring the end of the world. With his control other them removed, D'Kay then seemingly depowered Bacillus and others, before disappearing. But they in fact retained their powers. Years later Bacillus was killed in an explosion, orchestrated by a sentient virus from the Microverse that decided to kill everyone with power to control diseases.

baelroth.name: Baelroth
baelroth.origin: Baelroth is (presumably) an entity invoked as part of spell, including "Begone, Blight! Begone, Pestilence! In the names of Galigothiel and Baelroth, I abjure thee begone!", a spell intended to drive goblins from village grain stores. The spell was used by Doctor Strange to exorcise demonic entities tied to the Undying Ones, then, merging with Aradnea (who had been bred and mystically engineered to serve as a conduit for the Undying Ones), to banish all the Undying Ones possessing Atlanteans during the Fear.

bafomai.name: Bafomai
bafomai.origin: Circa 13,000 NC, after Queen Xaltana of Acheron tried to supplant the worship of Set, the Serpent-God, by the one of a Demon God, Bafomai was crowned king of Acheron after the wizard Kheperu convinced many lesser mages that Queen Xaltana was possessed and entombed her alive. When Hyborian rebels led by Mynas and accompanied by time-displaced Conan entered the royal palace, Bafomai managed to escape while Kheperu confronted the rebels, and was killed by Conan. Bafomai's ultimate fate remains unrevealed.

bags.name: Bags
bags.origin: Bags was a member of the Midnight Wreckers, a group of scavengers who assisted Gears Garvin in finding robotic components to help and fix robots during the robot revolution. After raiding the ruins of a Robowerx factory owned by Baintronics, the Midnight Wreckers were followed by a Baintronics roboticist named Rahman Bashara who wanted to help the fight for A.I. independence. In turn, a platoon of Bain-Robots trailed Bashara and attacked the base. Their attack coincided with an assault from the A.I. Army, who wrongfully believed Garvin to have been working against A.I.s. Bags fought against the Bain-Robots until Bashara disabled them. After the A.I. Army soldiers were convinced that their attack was misguided, the Midnight Wreckers parted ways with Gears and left the hideout, with Bashara having joined their ranks. Having decided to take an active role in the robot revolution, the Midnight Wreckers attacked a top-secret Baintronics site. They found a robot torture chamber where Bain scientists were experimenting on ways to keep robots subservient by simulation of pain. Their robotic victims asked the Midnight Wreckers to put them out of their misery, and Hassle granted them their wish.

bahkt.name: Bahkt
bahkt.origin: Bahkt was an old ally of Conan, turned enemy deranged by indulging in the potentially deadly drug Black Lotus. Leader of a bandit gang in Koth, Bahkt kidnapped Kobe and lured the Cimmerian into his forest hideout. As a freak sunburst abruptly occured in the middle of the night while they were battling, Bahkt escaped and Conan's second in command Shapur rescued Kobe. Bahkt was then approached by the Devourer of Souls, who gave him the power to consume the souls of men. Bahkt then began looking for Conan to steal his soul and fought Anneka, Kaleb, and Kobe, until he kidnapped Red Sonja to lure the Cimmerian. After having captured and abused the Hyrkanian warrior, Bakht left Sonja to be discovered by Conan's agents and returned to the Devourer of Souls, demanding more souls. With demonic power and the strength of ten man, Bahkt lured and attacked Conan in the Forest of the Eternal Verities, but he was eventually killed by the Cimmerian.

bahng.name: Bahng
bahng.origin: Bahng was a Fillian from Sakaar, and leader of the Doka'abi Clan. Once other tribes were united under the Warlord's rule, the Doka'abi Clan was chased into the desert. When the Warlord's forces demanded the Doka'abi Clan to run the Gauntlet, a challenge for survival, Bahng's clan attempted to contact the Hulk for help so he could represent his clan as their champion. Their call for help was heeded by Amadeus Cho, the successor of the late Bruce Banner. During the Gauntlet's second trial, the Hulk fought a robot that was using Doka'abi ally Elder Sharn and her two sons as a human shield. Bahng decided to jump into the arena floor to confront the Warlord, since he feared the Hulk was going to forfeit to spare Sharn and her sons, an act that would result in the Doka'abi Clan losing the Gauntlet, and he wanted die to fighting if the time for his people was to come. A guard warned Bahn that he had to return behind the arena's gate since only one champion was allowed at a time, but Bahng didn't heed his warning since the Hulk subsequently defeated the robot. While he was celebrating the Hulk's victory, Bahng was shot down by the guards. Bahng's moribund body was taken by the Hulk to the Doka'abi Clan's encampment, where he died after giving his people words of encouragement and naming Chak the new headman. Bahng's body was subsequently cremated in a funeral ceremony.

bai gu jing.name: Bai Gu Jing
bai gu jing.origin: Bai Gu Jing was a Ghost Rider of few words, but her actions spoke in volumes. A skilled fighter, Bai gave her all when the last of the Ghost Riders waged war against a corrupt Daniel Ketch and the Black Host–rogue angels in the service of Zadkiel. Unfortunately, even with the combined powers of her fellow warriors Molek, the Baron Skullfire and his lover, Marinette Bwa Chech, and the infamous Johnny Blaze, Bai Gu Jing was overcome by hellfire Avatars of Ketch, and her powers were forcibly stolen from her. It has yet to be revealed if she survived the process.

baiame.name: Baiame
baiame.origin: Baiame is the chief of the Aboriginal Australian gods of Australia. The Baiame myth tells how Baiame came down from the sky to the land, and created rivers, mountains, and forests. He then gave the people their laws of life, traditions, songs, and culture. He also created the first initiation site. This is known as a bora; a place where boys were initiated into manhood. When he had finished, he returned to the sky, and people called him the Sky Hero or All Father or Sky Father. He is married to Birrahgnooloo (Birran-gnulu), who is often identified as an emu, and with whom he has a son Daramulum (Dharramalan). It is believed he once lived on Earth as a mortal man before departing earth. The god Odin called upon him to meet with the other godheads of the pantheons of Earth to discuss the threat of the Celestials. Baiame later granted Thor a portion of the required life-energies to revive the Asgardians.

bailey.name: Bailey
bailey.origin: According to Bailey, she has "always had" her Bag of Infinite Capacity and its true origins remain unclear. Hellcat initially encountered Bailey shoplifting at the mall; however, Bailey avoided capture by teleporting via her Bag of Infinite Capacity. At some point, Bailey was recruited by Casiolena to aid in her conquest of Midgard. Casiolena promised to give Bailey magic and wipe out her student loans, in exchange, Bailey would recruit other newly powered individuals, such as Nuhumans and mutants, to Casiolena's cause. Casiolena quickly turned on Bailey when she was captured and led Hellcat and Valkyrie to her lair. Remorseful and penitent, Bailey left her life of crime and joined the Patsy Walker Temp Agency using her Bag of Infinite Capacity to aid in moving large furniture. After a combat training session with Hellcat and Jubilee, Attaché was abducted by Black Cat and forced to join a criminal gang. She was later rescued and freed from Black Cat's thrall by Hellcat, Jubilee, and Telekinian.

baird.name: Baird
baird.origin: Baird was a hypnotist for a travelling carnival where he mentally enslaved Leo Horne. After a year of being Baird's prisoner he eventually broke free enough to kill Baird and buried him in a field, however this left a permanent blood red mark on his shoulder. He bought a nostrum from Massu, a carnival salesman, who promises that it "will restore the flesh" and when he uses it, it removes the blood stain, but regenerates the body of Baird, who seemingly strangle Leo to death.

bakas.name: Bakas
bakas.origin: ===Soldier of Kamelia=== Bakas was a proud Kamelian soldier. At some occasion, Bakas found himself in Thule. There, he and his fellows encountered a water nymph, but were unable to slay her in spite of multiple attempts. ===Slave of Lemuria=== Under unrevealed circumstances, he was captured and became a galley slave aboard a Lemurian pirate galley. There he met with Kull, who thought him a madman for opposing the guards. By his provocation towards the guards and proudful acceptance of their beatings, Kull was reminded of the true meaning of freedom. The two befriended, Bakas calling Kull "little brother". One day, the galley was attacked by Cormorian pirates, and both Kull and Bakas were given weapons. Fighting too well, Bakas was wounded by his Lemurian tormentor, which was in turn slain by Kull, who fled to avoid vengeance. As the Lemurians needed all the slaves to save the cargo, Bakas was spared. ===Soldier of Valusia=== Years later, along with his new owner, Bakas went to the City of Wonders, Valusia. There, he forced his way into the Royal Palace to meet again with Kull. Kull was offered to buy Bakas but raged at the merchant and Valusian slavery laws alike. Councilor Tu bought Bakas' freedom nevertheless. Bakas became a soldier , captain, and close advisor of Kull. The water nymph Ala used her powers to sow strife among them. She eventually mesmerized Tu, then the Red Slayers into attacking Kull. Immune to her, Bakas knocked her out. On Bakas' advise, she was brought to be released into River Stagus by Brule, Kull and Bakas, An alternative tale has "Acuea" released in the sea near Kamula. Bakas was present when the crowd led by the usurper Ralim was met by Kull's fury. Bakas was able to quell Kull's rage, but not before many protesters were slain by the furious monarch. Brule, Kull and Bakas went on a vacation in Kamula, but the holiday was cut short by Brule, irritated by Bakas' and Kull's reminiscing their youth, urging Kull to resume to his duty. On the way home, they were attacked by the hordes of Ohris Dehjmal. Kull was wounded but despite their numbers, the Red Slayers, Brule and Bakas quickly routed the assailants. As Kull couldn't be moved, Bakas ordered the men to set up camp. Bakas urged to leave Kull to strike in force but Brule refused to have the Red Slayers attack. In fever dementia, Kull woke up and single-handedly repelled the enemy, rallying his troops. As Brule recognized Bakas' wisdom, the two put an end at their enmity. Later, Bakas stayed with Kull at the City of Wonders, when Brule brought him the news of the wiping out of Ohris Dehjmal's followers along with the head of an imposter. Bakas became friend with Cyrus. One night, Cyrus was attacked by thieves. When Bakas and the Red Slayers appeared on the scene, Cyrus was taken hostage by the brigands, but was savagely avenged by Kull, which Bakas highlighted, though Kull felt he had failed Cyrus.

fields.personality: Bakas was a proud one, referring the lash of the whip to accept being verbally abused by his Lemurian captors. Bakas was protected of the mesmerizing powers of the water nymphs, not being motivated in the ways of the flesh, or rather maybe because he was not interested in women. Bakas was more cool-headed than Kull.
fields.notes: Bakas appears in both versions of the story "Caresses of Mine Enemy", published in (March, 1989) and (November, 1993). In the first story, written by John Arcudi, Bakas resisted the mesmerism of the water nymph "Acuea" because he was "not solely motivated in the ways of the flesh". In the retelling of the story, written by Roy Thomas from Arcudi's plot, he instead resisted to "Ala" because of his homosexuality. In "The Savage Brotherhood", also in Savage Sword of Conan #215, Kull recounts a tale to "Kathonor". This character appears to be Bakas, with a similar appearance, the same background of Lemurian galley slave that eventually join Kull in Valusia, and calls him "little brother". It remains unknown whether Kathonor is supposed to be a distinct character, another name of Bakas, or simply an error.

bal cyphyro.name: Bal Cyphyro
bal cyphyro.first_appearance: The Mystic Hands of Doctor Strange (B&W) Vol 1 1
bal cyphyro.origin: Bal Cyphyro was a disciple of Dormammu. When he noticed Doctor Stephen Strange wondering around the Astral plane of the Dark Dimension, he was able to fend off any attack from the sorcerer and preceded to capture him, place him on his mighty demonic bull, and attempted to take him to his master, Dormammu. He did not care what his master chose to do with him because he served at the beck-and-call of his master. When they were close to Dormammu's domain, Stephen was able to use a minor spell to shift their trajectory just enough to fall into a pile Mindless Ones. They preceded to tear him and his bull apart, giving Strange a chance to escape.

balaal.name: Balaal
balaal.origin: Balaal's father Ossem was one of the great patriarchs of the Atlantean people. Balaal's brothers were killed by Atlantean barbarians and his father, a follower of the god Neptune, urged nonviolence. Balaal was the leader of a cult who worshiped the evil ancient god Set. Balaal's cult had built a device called the Golden Serpent to absorb their psychic energy in a bid to bring Set to Earth. When Balaal and his cult tried to sacrifice Ossem, Neptune smote the cult including Balaal, and protected Ossem.

balb.origin: Balb was part of the Carmondians of Carmondy IV. His life before the restoration is unknown but we can assume that he was married and had kids with Jara, and suicide when his god Veeda Leebre was imprisoned into the Desecration Annex by the Godstalker according to a Celestial decree. After the restoration, he was living with Jara and their two children, being an office-worker. Once the veil was uncovered on Veeda's manipulation and the manipulation faded by Genis-Vell's efforts. Balb seemingly returned to the death with his people.

balder.name: Balder
balder.origin: Balder the Brave was one of the Asgardians, an extra-dimensional race of beings once worshiped by the Vikings and Germans, as well as half-brother and close friend to Thor. Due to prophecies that Balder's death would help trigger the coming of Ragnarök, the destruction of Asgard and its inhabitants, Odin, ruler of Asgard, commanded his wife Frigga to make Balder invulnerable to harm. Before he allowed her to cast the spells, however, he accused Balder of treason, because during a battle with the Storm Giants, he had deserted the fight to put a bird who had fallen from its nest, back with its mother. Odin ordered his brothers Tyr and Honir to shoot arrows and throw lances at Balder, but the projectiles were stopped by an eagle and a plant. Seeing that Balder did not flinch, Odin was content that Balder was the bravest in all of Asgard and decided to grant him the invulnerability. left|thumb|200px|Young Balder Frigga cast spells that would protect Balder from harm by any living or inanimate thing while he was in the Asgardian dimension; however, Balder remained vulnerable to mistletoe. Loki, the god of mischief, learned of the prophecies and vulnerability, and tricked the blind god Hoder into firing an arrow tipped with mistletoe wood at Balder. Odin prevented Balder from actually dying, but when he was finally restored to life, his hair had turned white as a result from his experiences in Hel. Later, Balder's beloved, Nanna, sacrificed herself to save Balder from entrapment in marriage to Karnilla, and Balder was so distraught that he resolved never to speak of this incident or of her again. These experiences of death led Balder to forswear the life of a warrior and tried to forget his misery through eating, growing considerably fat. He rode to the desert to die, but encountered the Norns, three goddesses who oversaw the workings of destiny. The Norns gave Balder a vision that restored his faith, and he rode back to Asgard, eventually losing his excessive weight as he became a warrior again. Balder fought in many of Asgard's subsequent battles, including one against the demon Surtur, in which he needed to seek out the aid of the sorceress Karnilla. During a time when Odin had departed Asgard, Balder became the ruler of Asgard. Balder was killed during the final Ragnarok by an army wielding mistletoe-tipped spears. thumb|left Balder's spirit was pushed into the Destroyer by Loki and attacked Thor who was searching for the missing Asgardians. He was restored by Thor along with Loki and resided in Asgard Oklahoma. Balder replaced Thor as Lord of Asgard due to the sinister plans of Loki, and was convinced to move the Asgardians to Latveria, the domain of Doctor Doom, where they were placed at his mercy. Until the prompt arrival of Thor who brutally bested Dr. Doom's Destroyer freeing the Asgardians held prisoner including Balder. Once again ruler of Asgard yet broken in spirit Balder attempted to abdicate the throne. Thor convinced him not to. When the threat of the world eaters ensued over the nine realms Balder did not pursue any action despite the encroaching threat. Forcing Thor to resurrect Odin after which Balder departed Asgard with Tyr. Intent on dying a warrior's death to atone for the sins of failing to protect Asgard. Defeating many of the world eaters including Thane the prince of the Ano-Athnox before falling to their deaths. After the defeat and banishment of the Athnox to the Limbo in the World Tree, Balder's vengeful spirit was present along with Tyr. In Limbo, Balder's spirit became the leader of a group of fallen warriors sent by Hela to patrol the realm to keep its bestial inhabitants in check and prevent them from rising up. Balder's patrol served the additional purpose to deny one particular inhabitant of Limbo of prey: Surtur, the fire demon who grew in power by consuming its demon-kin. Balder left Limbo for a short while in order to interrupt a trial Thor was put on by Odin himself and speak in his brother's defense. Near the end of the entire universe as a consequence of the multiversal phenomena known as incursions, the King Loki of a possible future approached Hela in Hel to convince her to unleash Jormungand's spirit and trigger a new Ragnarok. Balder attempted to interrupt the alliance, but King Loki decapitated him. thumb|right|Balder as King of Hel When Odin's secret long-lost firstborn Angela set her sights on overthrowing Hela, Balder joined forces with Tyr and Skurge the Executioner in an attempt to quelch the rebellion, but they failed and were defeated. Angela became the new Queen of Hel after defeating Hela in combat. However, since she only wanted to use that power to set free the spirit of her lover Sera, she abdicated as soon as her true goal was achieved. She handed over the crown to Balder, and he became Hel's new regent. Not long afterwards, Niffleheim became the target of Muspelheim's new ruler, Sindr the Queen of Cinders, as part of an alliance between her realm and Ma

fields.notes: Balder's parentage has become a curious issue in Marvel Comics. According to traditional mythology, Balder was the son of Odin and his wife, Frigg. Although Marvel Comics occasionally acknowledged this in supplemental materials (such as the family tree in ), for decades Balder was mostly depicted as "Thor's friend" and not a prince of the realm. In , Balder's parentage was "revealed" to him and others seemingly for the first time. According to that story, Balder had always believed himself to be a foundling child, abandoned by his true parents and adopted by the royal court. In fact, he was the son of Odin and Frigga, initially abandoned because of Odin's premonitions about how Balder's death would lead to Ragnarok. The details of Balder's conception were confusing on their face. Although the story said Odin took Frigga into his bed, the implication was that Balder was born out of wedlock and Odin was in fact cheating on his wife when he bedded Frigga. Yet Frigga is and always has been presented as Queen of the Realm and Odin's wife. More recently, the details of Odin and Frigga's marriage were added to continuity in the Everything Burns crossover, indicating it was the result of a peace treaty between the Aesir and the Vanir, with the union of those two family lines securing the peace. In modern times, specifically stated Frigga was pregnant for the first time with a child of Odin, calling into question several previously presented sons including Balder, Tyr, and Hermod.
fields.trivia: When writing his series the New Gods over at DC Comics, Jack Kirby originally intended for Balduur, whose "living atoms" gave rise to the New Gods of New Genesis, to be the Asgardian Balder after the downfall of the Old Gods which bore heavy similarities to the Asgardians. The New Gods of Apokolips would've also been the descendants of Balder and Karnilla.

balder blake.origin: Balder Blake is the son of Thor and the Enchantress. On his eighteenth birthday, Blake made his third annual attempt to lift his father's hammer, Mjolnir, from its memorial, which was placed to mark the end of the Secret Wars. Even though he was still unworthy, his friends Crusader (Sarah Rogers), Mustang (CJ), Firefly (Matthew Storm), and Torrent (Kendall Logan) were still supportive of his efforts. While he and his friends helped to thwart his half-brother, Malefactor (Vincent von Doom) from his attempt to return to and conquer the original Earth, they found out that Crusader was worthy to wield Mjolnir. She was reluctant to, in deference to Blake's feelings about not being worthy himself, but she had to in order attempt the trip back to the original Earth, which was now possible due to the return of the self-exiled Hulk, and his new invention, which was based on the use of Mjolnir's dimensional portal opening abilities. The kids did not get back to Earth as they expected it on that trip; instead they found an Earth that was swarming with Sentinels. After they destroyed one of them, they decided to remain there and free that world as Avengers.

baldric.name: Baldric
baldric.origin: Baldric was a Viking sailor and warrior who lived in a fishing village in Norway circa 1000 AD. At some point, Baldric married a woman (whose name has never been revealed) who bore him a son, Cedaric. At some point, Baldric became enemies with a Vandal raider known as Garmund the Grim. Later, Baldric joined an expedition looking for treasure in the "New World" (actually the island of Greenland). During the voyage, Baldric became good friends with another warrior, Sigurd, who was secretly the god Thor who had been stripped of his powers and was posing as a mortal as part of a wager he had made with his villainous half-brother Loki. Baldric repeatedly impressed Thor with his strength and courage, far beyond what Thor had expected from a mere mortal. Although two of the expedition's five ships were lost in a storm that Loki had secretly created, the three remaining ships made it to their destination. While some of the landing party foraged for food, Baldric and Sigurd led a group assigned to explore the ruins that were visible from the beach. However, Loki had already used his magic to secretly set deadly traps within the long-deserted Atlantean outpost, and the Viking treasure-hunters encountered magically-enlarged giant rats that slew or wounded some of them. Once the rats were destroyed, Baldric, Sigurd and two others went searching for a way out, but instead found a crypt full of mummies who came alive and attacked them. Baldric fought well against the mummies until one of them managed to stab him in the back. Fatally wounded, Baldric expired in Thor's arm, never knowing he had befriended a god. His death inspired "Sigurd" to lead the surviving Vikings to prevail against Loki's undead warriors and, when Loki showed his hand by transforming a lizard into a dragon, Thor was released from his oath, enabling him to regain his godly powers and use them to defeat the dragon. Later, after returning to Asgard, Thor was sure that a soul as noble and courageous as Baldric was even then enjoying the fruits of his valor in Valhalla. Ten years later, Thor returned to that Norwegian village to check on Baldric's son. "Sigurd" was surprised to discover that Cedaric was a pacifist who had no respect for his father, regarding him as a man whose greed for treasure had left his wife a penniless widow. Despite his pacifism, Cedaric allowed "Sigurd" to train him in the ways of the warrior and proved to be quite skilled. When the training was completed, "Sigurd" gave Baldric's sword "Skullcrusher" to Cedaric, claiming that he had promised Baldric that he would give it to Cedaric when he came of age. Although Cedaric thought the sword was beautiful and a fine example of the swordsmith's art, he refused to accept it. Later, when his father's enemy Garmund threatened the village, Cedaric was able to use his intelligence and bravery to non-violently force Garmund to leave the village (mostly) undamaged and the villagers unharmed.

baldwin drake.name: Baldwin Drake
baldwin drake.origin: Baldwin Drake was the owner of the Drake Lumber Company. After losing a government bid to purchase the Burton County forest to Borden Lumber Co, he would hire criminals to set the forest on fire. Unfortunately for Baldwin, John Borden -- owner of Borden Lumber -- was an old colleague of Professor Philo Zog, inventor of the Electro robot. After setting the blaze, Drake would be angered to see the robot attempting to put out the flames. He would send his thugs to shoot Borden and capture Zog, tossing the scientist into the inferno. Borden would survive the attack and use Electro to save Zog, and both men would put out the blaze and send Electro to capture Drake. Drake and his men would fortify his lumber mill, but it's defenses would be incapable of stopping the robot who would easily capture them as they attempted to escape in a getaway car.

balin.name: Balin
balin.origin: Balin is a Galadorian, the first born son of Rom and Brandy Clark of Earth and wields the armor of Terminator. He was the presumed heir of the mantle of Prime Director of Galador after the disappearance and apparent death of his father. However, when he presented himself to his father's sentient weapon Axadar, he was rejected because of his innate anger. Afterward, Balin would lead the Spaceknights to the planet Trion to quell the rebellion there. The mission was initially very successful but ended in disaster with the death of Lightningbolt at the hands of the new enemy Wraithknights. Balin's anger would soon cause an incident with the Galadorian Vanguard and he disobeyed orders to stand down confronting the enemy and their leader the Supreme Wraithknight. The squad would be saved when Axadar miraculously appeared and bonded to Balin's brother Tristan who then used Galador's greatest weapon to slay a monstrous Deathwing. Balin was among the Spaceknights that assisted Nova, Quasar (Phyla-Vell) and Blastaar against the Annihilation Wave. Balin resurfaced as part of a group of heroes called by Mister Fantastic in the Negative Zone to fight the forces of the Cancerverse led by the Sentry.

She was so impressed with his wisdom that she gifted him gold, jewels, and spices, and the two became lovers. Balkis was trained as a sorceress and upon Solomon's death, she succeeded him as the Sorcerer Supreme, serving between 800 BC and 550 BC.

ballista grim.name: Ballista Grim
ballista grim.origin: === Working for Thanos === Ballista Grim was a member of the Butcher Squadron, a team of killers that worked for Thanos to carry out acts of wanton murder and death. One job she was a part of was wiping out the pacifistic Dorcaernir people. Later, she and Butcher Squadron were ordered to attack the planet of Zen-Whoberi to prevent the planet from being taken over by the Universal Church of Truth. When Thanos took an interest in a young Zen-Whoberi named Gamora, Ballista's fellow Butcher Squadron member Ebony Maw allowed Gamora to escape. When Thanos questioned the Squadron on who allowed her to escape, Ballista and the Squadron refused to talk. To keep the Squadron in line, Thanos killed one of its members, Infesti Macera. After a mission on the planet of Sakaar, which they considered pointless, Butcher Squadron members began to question Thanos's leadership. Blood Brothers and three pilots were encouraged by the Squadron to hold Gamora for ransom. However, Gamora fought back and defeated her kidnappers. Ballista and the rest of the Squadron avoided the punishment by feigning loyalty toward Thanos. However, they still didn't give up on their plan to betray Thanos. After Gamora threatened to tell Thanos about their betrayal, Ballista and Proxima Midnight decided to kill Gamora. The resulting chaos led to a full-scale mutiny. Thanos threatened them into quelling the mutiny and left the Sanctuary to deal with his arch-nemesis, Magus. With Thanos gone, the Butcher Squadron once again tried to kill Gamora. However, Gamora was able to get to a ship. Ballista attempted to get Gamora out of the ship. However, Gamora took off with Ballista still on top of the ship. Ballista fell and ended up drifting in the void without a spacesuit. ===Peaceful Life=== In the end, Ballista settled down on the planet of Mahn Zyly. Her normal life there was, however, interrupted when one of her neighbors brought in amnesiac Nebula. Being wary of her based on their previous encounters and unaware of her amnesiac state, Ballista immediately attacked Nebula.

balo.name: Balo
balo.origin: Balo, a resident of the planet of Sakaar, was a Haarg, a descendant of the human gamma mutate Amadeus Cho. He and his sister Tala were forced to go into hiding when the Grand Priestess Venkiera began wiping out the Haarg, blaming them for the trouble plaguing Sakaar. One day, Venkiera's men captured Balo, forcing Tala to ask their grandfather Amadeus Cho for help. Cho agreed, and he and Tala discovered that Balo was one of many Haarg children captured by Venkiera. Cho and Tala were forced to flee when they were attacked by Venkiera's Sentinels. Cho and Tala later staged a rescue mission with help from Korg and Jen Walters. Balo and the other Haarg children were freed, but then Venkiera revealed that the children were actually bait to lure Cho from hiding so he would bring her the Hulk so Venkiera could use his gamma energy to power a doomsday weapon to wipe from the Haarg from Sakaar by destroying the planet. The Hulk wasn't there, so, Venkiera used Jen Walters as a substitute. After Jen was freed by Cho, Balo and the others helped evacuate civilians to Sky City. After Cho used his gamma energy to keep Sky City afloat for a while, they arrived at the home of Hulk and convinced him to rescue Sakaar. Using his intelligence, Cho located Venkiera's doomsday machine, and Banner destroyed it. However, the machine's true function was to stop the spinning of Sakaar's molten core, leaving the planet vulnerable to cosmic rays that the core's magnetic field fended off as part of Venkiera's insane plan to cleanse Sakaar by killing everyone, including herself. Banner was fortunately able to jump-start the core's spin by striking it. With Sakaar saved, everyone began making peace with Balo helping Banner open up.

baltag.name: Baltag
baltag.origin: Baltag was the commander of Kang's elite guard, who rose against him after the invasion of King Carelius' realm, for not slaying Princess Ravonna, as the murder of all conquered monarchs was a common practice, in order to prevent them from ever leading a rebellion. Baltag took control of the rest of the generals, who tried to assassinate Kang, but he teamed up with the Avengers and managed to squash the coup. As Kang was sending the Avengers back to their time, the defeated Baltag leapt out and fired a shot at Kang. Captain America tried to warn him, but Ravonna leapt in the way and was shot herself. Baltag was eventually killed by Kang's guards.

balthakk.name: Balthakk
balthakk.origin: ===Origin=== Balthakk was a being of pure energy, and one of the principalities, entities invoked for power. Balthakk himself was invoked for its destructive energy bolts. Very little is known of Balthakk's origin, though, like virtually all of the Principalities, Balthakk was presumably of extradimensional origin. He ruled over the dimension of Balthakk, located at the edges of the plane of Watoomb, within the Archipelago of Anguish and Redemption. Balthakk was one of the eight mystical principalities who entered into the Octessence pact, claiming to be the most powerful among them yet wishing to avoid an open conflict. In their stead, they would empower each one an Exemplar (avatar) to fight for them. The Exemplar's candidate was to discover the Blinding Brazier of Balthakk in a temple in Nunavut territory near Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada. ===Modern Age=== ====War of the Seven Spheres==== Like all the members of Octessence, Balthakk participated in the conflict known as the War of the Seven Spheres which lasted five-thousand years (waged within months by human reckoning). ====Wager of the Octessence==== His Brazier of Balthakk was used to empower Samantha McGee as his Exemplar, Inferno.

balthar.name: Balthar
balthar.origin: Balthar was a sorcerer and practitioner of black magic during the 1940s. In winter of 1942 he became so fed up with the local children which were harassing him that he left his home to study in solitude upon the nearby Bald Mountain. Seeking to summon the devil to attain ultimate power, Balthar used his magical skills to summon a creature calling itself Satan. Satan granted Balthar more power and the ability to kill with his eyes and gifted him with the Lamp of Evil, in exchange for which Balthar had to become his emissary on Earth and bring him the greatest champion of good. Balthar, grateful of his new master's gifts, agreed to follow his orders. After Satan returned to his realm, Balthar used his crystal ball to conjure up the image of the man his master sought and was surprised to find that it was the costumed hero Captain America and then began a plot to lure the hero to him. Balthar descended from his mountain solitude and used his death stare to start a murder spree around Camp Lehigh attracting the attention of Captain America and his partner Bucky. Finding that the murder spree was not working fast enough, Balthar found a den of crooks hoping that they would lead him to Captain America. As fate would have it, Cap and Bucky were searching underworld hideouts and happened upon the crooks den shortly after Balthar made his arrival and convinced the gang to work with him. During the fight between Cap, Bucky and the mobsters Balthar left leaving behind his Lamp of Evil. When the fight was over, the Lamp suddenly disappeared in a flash of light, which made the heroes so tired that they camped out in a nearby bait-man's hut. As they slept, Balthar kidnapped Bucky and left a note for Captain America challenging him to a duel for the boys life on Bald Mountain. Awakening, Cap found the note and rushed after his young sidekick. There, Captain America battled Balthar, and when the villain was losing he attempted to use his death stare on the hero. However, Captain America blocked the sorcerer's gaze with his shield and its reflective surface redirected Balthar's death gaze back upon him, killing him instantly. However, even in death Balthar completed his part of the bargain: bringing Captain America to Bald Mountain, and here Captain America battle with the creature calling himself Satan, a battle the hero managed to win.

balu.name: Balu
balu.origin: Balu the Tiger was the faithful companion of the jungle adventurer known as Trojak and would often accompany him on his adventures. When Trojak was sent out into the jungle to discover his own people by his tribe, Balu accompanied him, aiding Trojak in getting Edith Alton and her companions out of the jungle alive. Later, Balu aided Trojak in killing a prehistoric monster that was attacking their village, and later in rescuing Edith from an armed Nazi camp. Balu later rescued Trojak, Edith, and her brother Jerry (an Allied spy) from the Nazis by setting off explosives planted earlier by Jerry. Later, when Jerry took ill, Balu followed Trojak and Edith on their quest to obtain the nectar of the Devil-Flower to cure him. During this quest, Balu helped Trojak and Edith fend off attacks from the Gemba Tribe who worshiped the plant. During their escape, Balu sabotaged the Gembian boats, leaving them unable to pursue them further. Balu's subsequent activities remain unrevealed.

balus.name: Balus
balus.origin: Balus was a tribal leader who would kidnap Anna Twisdon, daughter of Lord Twisdon, to make her his peoples "white goddess". Forcing her to comply through hypnosis, Balus would face Dakor the Magician, a friend of the Twisdons, who had come to rescue Anna from his clutches. Although Balus would have Dakor tossed into the Pool of Nordu (which would nullify the heroes powers) and have him tossed into a raging fire, Dakor would save himself when the heat from the flames would evaporate the water. In their final clash, Balus would be tossed into the blaze and burn alive. Upon Balus' death, Anna would be freed from his control and returned to her father.

balzor.name: Balzor
balzor.origin: Balzor was a member of a space pirate crew led by Sklarr. However, Sklarr was defeated, killed and replaced by Gray Gargoyle, who became the new captain; Balzor was the first to agree to follow the Gargoyle. Balzor became a crewman in the Gargoyle's warship and handled the slaves in the cosmic furnaces. When the Gargoyle captured and enslaved Thor and several Asgardians, they were sent to work in the furnaces. Balzor harassed them along with other slaves such as Gormok, but when Asgardian Hogun stood to Balzor, Balzor was intimidated and allowed Hogun to help Gormok. When crewman Fee-Lon staged a mutiny against the Gargoyle, Balzor was not seen in the fight. The mutiny was stopped by the Asgardians, and both Fee-Lon and the Gargoyle were apparently killed; the Asgardians ensured that the surviving pirates would amend their ways.

bambi.name: Bambi
bambi.origin: "Bambi" was a baby deer that was saved from hunters by the Hulk, who named the fawn after the popular from the Disney film of the same name. The fawn was kept at Dr. Strange's Sanctum Sanctorum and became the Hulk's pet. It later had its brain switched with that of Chondu the Mystic who, angered at having his brain transplanted into the body of a baby deer, tried to thwart the Defenders as best he could. It was kidnapped by the Ludberdites and attacked Jack Norriss (inhabiting Nighthawk's body) when he arrived in their prison. Chondu's mind was transferred into a new composite body by Arthur Nagan, the leader of the Headmen, much to his chagrin. The fate of Bambi is unknown, as the deer was not recovered by the Defenders and, by that time, the Hulk had lost interest in the animal.

bambi long.origin: A woman that, alongside Jake Miller and Ralph Bunker, stole a shop and killed its owner, and later went to a bar to drink. When the three leave the bar, Jake drives drunk and the three die when the car falls in a broken road. bambina arbogast.name: Bambina Arbogast
bambina arbogast.origin: ===Early Years=== Mrs. Bambina Arbogast began her administrative career in US Army services, acting as clerk to a mobile army surgical hospital unit, then spent 10 years in the US Department of Defense. ===Stark International=== In the next stage of her career, she interviewed for a position as executive assistant to Tony Stark, head of Stark International. While waiting for Stark to arrive for the interview in his office, Mrs. Arbogast was caught in the midst of a battle between Iron Man and the villain Whirlwind. Unaware that Stark himself was Iron Man, Mrs. Arbogast refused to run; instead she calmly managed incoming calls on Stark's phone and helped rescue items in the office from damage in the fight. Ultimately, Whirlwind was beaten when Mrs. Arbogast distracted him with the telephone, granting Iron Man the opportunity to knock him unconscious. Iron Man returned to his identity as Tony Stark and promptly hired Mrs. Arbogast without an interview, impressed with her capabilities. Mrs. Arbogast became one of Stark's most important employees in his later days at Stark International and was also a friend to fellow employees such as James Rhodes. When Stark International was set ablaze during a battle between Iron Man and Blacklash, Mrs. Arbogast risked her life trying to rescue Stark's personal papers from the flames. ===Resilient=== When Tony reinvented his company in Stark Resilient, he hired Bambi again, who at that moment was a millionaire investor.

bamboo knife butcher.name: Bamboo Knife Butcher
bamboo knife butcher.origin: thumb|left|129px|Mr. Smallen Mr. Smallen was related to the Mallon family, a wealthy family who in the 1940s owned a number of successful mines in various remote parts of the world. Smallen regularly traveled to these mines and soon became immersed in the culture of the local savages that were indigenous to the regions where the Mallon mines were located. Becoming completely indoctrinated in the anti-white ways of the local savages, Smallen managed to convince them into letting him join their tribe. Ultimately, Smallen had been driven completely insane and came up with a plot to try and eliminate all whites. To this end, he returned to the United States with a number of locals to carry out this plot. With his followers operating under the guise of working staff hired at the Mallon estate, Smallen and his men organized the kidnapping of Jim Mallon Jr, the youngest of the family who when on many expeditions. As Jim was en route on another expedition, Smallen then mailed a shrunken head to the Mallon home to convince them that Jim was dead, but instead decided for reasons that only made sense to himself, he decided to keep Jim alive a while long and kept him prisoner within his Manhattan penthouse apartment. Meanwhile, Jim's mother Mrs. Mallon, not believing that her son is dead then sent out a call to Captain America on a radio program. Hearing this, Captain America came to the Mallon estate with his partner Bucky. There they were introduced to Smallen and the work staff, unaware of their implication in the disappearance of Jim. When Captain America noticed that the mailing address on the package containing the shrunken head was complete, it prompted Smallen to send his men to attack the hero and his sidekick as they left the Mallon property. While the two heroes were busy fighting off their attackers, Smallen rushed to his penthouse apartment. Eventually, Captain America and Bucky followed Smallen's minions to his home and soon were captured once again and brought before Smallen. Smallen revealed his motivations. But before he could behead Cap, Bucky and Jim, Cap broke free and fought back. While Bucky and Jim fought off Smallen's minions, Cap and Smallen took their fight to the roof of the building. There, Smallen was knocked off the roof and fell to his death. His minions were then easily defeated thereafter and Jim explained how his uncle had gone insane.

ban duckley.name: Ban Duckley
ban duckley.origin: Ban Duckley is the Publisher of Marble Comics. When Abomination and M.O.D.O.K. showed up at his office threatening him and the Editor in Chief Moe Kesado because in the comics they were portrayed as idiots who were always doomed to lose, Moe replied that they were not the ones making the decisions, but that it was the job of the editor Blate Nosby. Ban confirmed what Moe had said and added that they at Marble Comics were in charge of making the important decisions, such as which character to get on the underoos.

ban ki moon.name: Ban Ki-moon
ban ki moon.origin: When a sea monster emerged from the East River between Manhattan and Queens in New York City, the Secretary-General of the United Nations, Ban Ki-moon, called upon Hercules to handle the situation. Ban Ki-moon later visited the Triskelion, the headquarters of the Ultimates, and expressed the worries of some U.N. member states about the recent cooperation between Wakanda and the United States of America to King T'Challa, stating their alliance could extend to the military arena. T'Challa dismissed Ban's claims as unfounded fears, and stated that the United States would only slow Wakanda down.

ban luck.name: Ban-Luck
ban luck.origin: Ban-Luck was the contact agent of G.R.A.M.P.A. for Avenger members U.S. Agent and Quicksilver during a mission-op in China. The problem was with a group of Alpha Primitives led by the mysterious Inhuman The Unspoken who came out of exile for conquest. As Ban-Luck and U.S. Agent tried to understand who this person was, they were confronted by the People's Defense Force who started to attack them and The Unspoken for their trespass into their country. During the ongoing battle, Ban-Luck and Agent were rescued by four different Avenger teams, Iron Patriot's team, the Young Avengers, Ronin's group and Hank Pyms. With so many heroes fighting him, and the return of Quicksilver to the battle persuaded him that this was not worth his time, so he decided to go back to where he came from. As everyone left Ban-Luck filed her report to her superiors on the success of the mission.

banapur khan.name: Banapur Khan
banapur khan.origin: Banapur Khan was an Indonesian pirate hired by the Cult of the Black Blade to help them obtain the Muramasa Blade. He captured Kojima Noburo, the secretary of the blade's owner Mariko Yashida, and tried to torture information out of him, to no avail. Yashida sent her beloved, Wolverine, to rescue Noburo, but he arrived too late to save the secretary's life and fought Banapur to avenge him. Banapur was no match for Wolverine and almost escaped, but was killed by a stewardess from Noburo's plane who had stowed away on Banapur's speedboat.
